## How to read this document

**Provenance tags.** Every design element names the draft(s) it came from: `[A]`, `[B]`, `[C]`, `[L]` for a change the lead made during the v1 merge, `[R1:<finding id>]` for a change made in response to review round 1 (for example `[R1:SEC-r1-01]`) and `[R2:<finding id>]` for a change made in response to review round 2 (for example `[R2:BA-r2-06]`). A bare `[R1]` or `[R2]` marks a table row or paragraph whose finding ids are given inline, and `[R1:<reviewer> decision]` or `[R2:<reviewer> decision]` marks a change that answers a reviewer's proposed user decision rather than a finding (§17.1). `[R2:<reviewer> observation on <finding id>]` marks a change that answers an observation a round-2 reviewer attached to the status of an earlier finding (the ledger's prior-finding table); an observation is not a finding and has no id of its own. The decision log (section 16) records the alternatives rejected and why; the review ledger (`ledger.md`) records every finding and its resolution. `v1`, `v2` and `v3` always mean design versions; library releases are written `1.0` and `1.x`.

The `tmp-*` experiment directories named above were temporary and no longer exist; treat their results as recorded findings, and re-run an experiment before relying on it for a new decision.

**LEAD-EXP-1** (`tmp-lead/exp-gql-denial.cjs`, Nest 11.1.17, @nestjs/apollo 13.2.4, Express, Node 22.22.0). Result for a guard-thrown denial:

| Thrown object                                                 | 401 code          | 403 code    | 429 code                    | Logged at ERROR by Nest |
| ------------------------------------------------------------- | ----------------- | ----------- | --------------------------- | ----------------------- |
| `HttpException` subclass with `extensions` (draft B)          | `UNAUTHENTICATED` | `FORBIDDEN` | **`INTERNAL_SERVER_ERROR`** | no                      |
| `IntrinsicException` subclass with `extensions` (this design) | `UNAUTHENTICATED` | `FORBIDDEN` | `RATE_LIMITED`              | no                      |
| plain `GraphQLError` (drafts A, C)                            | `UNAUTHENTICATED` | `FORBIDDEN` | `RATE_LIMITED`              | **yes, every denial**   |

**LEAD-EXP-2** (`tmp-revise-v2/exp-fastify-child-errhandler.cjs`, Nest 11.1.17 and 12.0.1 × `NestFactory` and `@nestjs/testing`, Fastify 5.8.2/5.12.1, global prefix `v1`) `[R1:NEST-r1-04]`. An encapsulated auth plugin registered with `await` in `onModuleInit` sets a child error handler that reads `root.errorHandler` **at request time**. Result on all four runs: a throwing auth handler reached the app's `APP_FILTER` (status 599 written by the filter); an over-limit body answered the canonical `413 { code: 'PAYLOAD_TOO_LARGE' }` with the root `onRequest`-set CORS header preserved; a controller error still reached the filter.

**LEAD-EXP-3** (`tmp-revise-v2/exp-coordinator-last-arrival.cjs`, Nest 11.1.17 and 12.0.1) `[R1:NEST-r1-02, NEST-r1-03]`. A coordinator that records the adapter from `init$` and receives platforms from a provider behind an **async** dependency calls `prepare()` when both are known. `NestFactory.create`: `init$ → platforms registered → prepare → create() resolved → init()`. `@nestjs/testing`: `platforms registered → compile() resolved → init$ → prepare → createNestApplication() returned`. `createApplicationContext` and `createMicroservice`: `init$ adapter=null → skip`, no throw.

**LEAD-EXP-4** (`tmp-revise-v2/exp-node-fetch-headers.mjs`, Node 22.22.0) `[R1:SEC-r1-01]`. A server-side `fetch` POST carries `sec-fetch-mode: cors` and **no** `Origin`, `Referer` or `Sec-Fetch-Site`.

**LEAD-EXP-5** (`tmp-finish-v2/exp5/`, TypeScript 5.9.3, 6.0.3 and 7.0.2 × `nodenext` ESM, `nodenext` CJS, `bundler`, `node16` CJS). A fake package with this design's exports map keeps `PrincipalKinds` in a shared declaration chunk that the root entry re-exports. Its `./api-key` declaration file augments the **root specifier by package self-reference** (`declare module '<own name>' { interface PrincipalKinds { 'api-key': … } }`). Result on all 24 runs: a consumer that imports `./api-key` gets `'api-key'` in `PrincipalKind` and narrowing on `p.kind`; a consumer that imports only the root does not. Negative control: with the augmentation pointed at a wrong module name, the consumer fails to compile while the package's own declarations stay silent under `skipLibCheck`, so only a consumer fixture can catch a broken augmentation (§12.9 step 10).

**LEAD-EXP-6** (`tmp-finish-v2/drizzle/probe.mjs`, Node 24.14.1; constructor copied verbatim from drizzle-orm 0.45.2 `errors.js:10-19`) `[R1:SEC-r1-08]`. A `DrizzleQueryError` has the enumerable own properties `query`, `params` and `cause`. Wrapped as a `cause`, `util.inspect` prints the query parameter (a session token) twice: once in the message and once in `params`. After scrubbing `message` and `stack` **in place** it still prints it once, and a JSON serializer over the error's own properties prints it once as well. A redacted cause therefore has to be a new error built from an allow-list of fields (§13.4, ADR-43).

**LEAD-EXP-7** (`tmp-close-gaps-r2/exp7/probe2.mjs`, `probe3.mjs`; Node 24.14.1, @apollo/server 4.13.0, Mercurius 16.10.0 on Fastify 5, graphql 16.14.2; `NODE_ENV` production and development) `[R1:SEC-r1-19]`. A resolver throws an error that no transport mapped, as a param decorator does when the guard did not run. With the detail in `message`, both drivers send the handler name and the hint to the client in `errors[0].message`, in both modes. With a fixed generic `message`, the detail and hint in ordinary own properties (`detail`, `hint`, `code`) and `extensions: { code, reason, statusCode }`, neither driver sends the detail or the hint; both copy `extensions` (Apollo adds its own `stacktrace` in development, whose header line is the generic message). `util.inspect`, which Nest's logger uses (LEAD-V31), prints the enumerable `detail` and `hint`.

## 0. Summary and principles

### 0.1 Summary

better-auth defines its own integration contract. Its handler is a Web-standard `handler(Request): Promise<Response>`. Framework bridging is done by plugins (`nextCookies`, `sveltekitCookies`, `tanstackStartCookies`, `expo`), server code calls `auth.api.*`, and authorization runs on access control. This design binds NestJS to exactly that contract and reimplements nothing better-auth already does. It has three parts:

1. **The `nestjs()` better-auth plugin** `[A][B][C]`. The user adds it last to `betterAuth({ plugins })`, following the `nextCookies()` precedent, and a boot check makes it mandatory. It is the only code that runs inside better-auth's pipeline, and it does five things:
   - bridges Nest hook providers and database hooks, preserving better-auth's return-value semantics per operation;
   - forwards `Set-Cookie` from the library's own `auth.api.*` calls (principal sources and policies) into the current response. Application code's direct calls are forwarded only in handlers that opt in, and only when the call used the caller's own credential or none `[R1:BA-r1-02, SEC-r1-03]`;
   - suppresses session refresh on any endpoint dispatched from a cookie-less scope, which also covers the stateless refresh-cache branch;
   - declares an unguessable client-IP header, random per plugin instance and never leaving the process, through `init()` `[R1:SEC-r1-18]`;
   - records which answers an endpoint itself produced, as opposed to a before-hook short-circuit, so that an authoritative identity read accepts exactly the sessions better-auth's own admin and sensitive endpoints accept `[R2:BA-r2-06]`.

   It imports only `better-auth/api`, `better-auth/cookies` and `defu`, never `@nestjs/*`, so the better-auth CLI can still load `auth.ts`.

2. **A small kernel** `[B][C]`: the module, guard, scope interceptor, principal resolver, authorization evaluator, origin check, boot validator and error model. It depends only on its own extension contracts and on better-auth's public surface. It never branches on a platform, transport, principal-kind or policy name; the data it compares (principal kinds, credential header names) is supplied by extensions.
3. **Extension units** `[A][B][C]` for the five extension points:
   - HTTP platforms: Express and Fastify ship; third parties plug in their own;
   - transports: HTTP, GraphQL (Apollo and Mercurius), WebSockets (socket.io and ws), and RPC;
   - principal sources: the better-auth session, API keys, or a third party's;
   - authorization policies: thin adapters over better-auth's permission APIs;
   - hook providers.

   Built-in units register through exactly the same contract a third party uses. Their behavior is proven identical by runner-agnostic conformance kits shipped in `./testing/conformance`.

**Auth routes.** Every request under better-auth's own mount path, for every method, goes to `auth.handler`. The platform produces a Web `Request` with the exact body bytes, a trust-proxy-aware origin and client IP, and HTTP/2-safe headers. It writes the `Response` back verbatim: status, every `Set-Cookie`, redirects and streams. The Express binding uses two phases: bounded raw capture once the HTTP adapter and the platform are both known (inside `NestFactory.create()` / `createNestApplication()`), then dispatch at `onModuleInit`, after the user's CORS and middleware. The Fastify binding is an encapsulated plugin with a `parseAs: 'buffer'` catch-all parser, a body limit, and a child error handler that hands failures to Nest's error pipeline.

**App routes and messages.** A single transport-neutral guard resolves the principal lazily, at most once per logical request (and per connection where the transport opts in). It calls `auth.api.getSession({ headers, returnHeaders: true })` and forwards only `set-cookie`, and only where the transport can carry cookies. Principals that act for a user with a narrower grant (API keys, OAuth tokens) are admitted only on routes that name their kind. Unsafe operations whose browser leg carries a cookie pass better-auth's own origin rule, whatever credential authenticated them `[R2:SEC-r2-01]`. Authorization then runs through requirement expressions whose policies travel by reference in route metadata, and every decision is made per handler invocation.

**The common case** needs three lines plus one platform import:

```ts
// auth.ts: static and CLI-friendly; imports no Nest code
export const auth = betterAuth({ database, emailAndPassword: { enabled: true },
  plugins: [admin(), organization(), nestjs()] });                    // nestjs() last
declare module 'nestjs-slightly-better-auth' { interface Register { auth: typeof auth } }

// app.module.ts
@Module({ imports: [BetterAuthModule.forRoot({ auth, platforms: [expressPlatform()] })] })
export class AppModule {}

// any controller: no generics, typed from `typeof auth`
@Get('me') me(@CurrentSession() s: AuthSession) { return s.user.role; }
@RequireOrgPermission({ project: ['delete'] }, { organization: fromParam('orgId') })   // typo = compile error
@Delete(':orgId/projects/:id') remove() {}
@Public() @Get('health') health() {}                                                   // zero auth I/O
```

The user never sets `bodyParser: false`, never adds `hooks: {}` placeholders, writes no generics at use sites, and gets no CORS side effects.

### 0.2 How the design embodies better-auth's philosophy (R1)

| better-auth principle (R:ba-core §1.1)                                             | How this design honors it                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                     |
| ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| P1/P2: framework-agnostic; the Web `Request → Response` handler is the single seam | Auth routes are raw platform routes that call `auth.handler` with a `Request` we build (§6). No auth endpoint is re-declared as a Nest controller. Routing, 404/415, the origin/CSRF check **for auth routes**, rate limiting, `disabledPaths` and plugin `onRequest`/`onResponse` all stay inside `auth.handler`. better-auth's origin check is router-only (LEAD-V16), so the cookie-carrying surfaces this library creates (app routes, GraphQL mutations, WebSocket handshakes, GraphQL operations over a WebSocket) get the same rule applied by the kernel, with better-auth's own trusted-origin set, matcher and disable flags, and without exemptions better-auth does not make (§7.10) `[R1:SEC-r1-01, BA-r1-03]` `[R2:SEC-r2-01, SEC-r2-03]`.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      |
| P3/P4: plugin-first; customize inside the pipeline with hooks                      | Everything that must run _during_ a better-auth call enters through the `nestjs()` plugin, added at construction (§10). `auth.options` is never mutated (S1).                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                 |
| P5: type safety through inference                                                  | Types flow from `typeof auth` through a `Register` augmentation, which is better-auth's own `BetterAuthPluginRegistry` idiom. Permission arguments, hook contexts, DB hook payloads and endpoint paths are inferred from better-auth's own option and endpoint types (§11). Core accepts a structural `AuthLike`, never bare `Auth`.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          |
| P6: server code calls `auth.api`                                                   | The session principal comes from `auth.api.getSession` (§7). Policies call `userHasPermission`, `hasPermission`, `getActiveMemberRole` and `role().authorize()` (§8). API keys are verified by `verifyApiKey`. Nothing parses session cookies for authentication or queries the database itself (the API-key outage probe is a health check: one read and one no-op write of a random id, §8.3.1).                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            |
| P8: secure by default                                                              | The global guard is on by default. `@Public()` performs zero auth I/O. Delegated principals (API keys, OAuth tokens) are admitted only where a route names them, and built-in policies never widen them beyond their own grant (Z5). Unsafe operations that carry a cookie must come from a trusted origin, as on better-auth's own routes. `Origin`, `Referer`, `Sec-Fetch-*`, `Cookie`, `Authorization` and `Content-Type` are never rewritten. The client IP is trust-proxy-aware and anti-spoofed, and a production app with no `baseURL` fails boot. Auth-route bodies are bounded. Bad credentials are never downgraded to anonymous. Infrastructure failures are 5xx and are logged with credentials redacted. Every handler a transport serves must be reachable by the guard when it declares something or its transport requires it for every handler (B16), and every handler carrying library metadata must be served by a transport, or boot fails (WebSocket gateways on every Nest major, hybrid RPC handlers, GraphQL field resolvers that carry requirements, forgotten transports, `globalGuard: false`) `[R2:NEST-r2-02]`. Misconfiguration fails at compile time or boot. |
| P10: framework cookie bridging is a plugin                                         | The `nestjs()` after-hook, gated on `ctx._flag !== 'router'`, forwards `Set-Cookie` of direct calls where forwarding is enabled. This is the `nextCookies` pattern (`BA/integrations/next-js.ts:47-144`, LEAD-V14). As with `nextCookies`, forwarding for application code is a deliberate opt-in; it is not a side effect of adding the plugin `[R1:BA-r1-02]`.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              |
| P11: ESM-first                                                                     | ESM is the canonical build. The exports map is `module-sync`-first, so on the supported Node range a single ESM copy serves both `import` and `require` (§12).                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                |
| "Do not reimplement" (R:ba-core §9)                                                | Not reimplemented: routing, auth-route CSRF, rate limiting, body parsing of auth routes, cookie names and parsing (`better-auth/cookies`), permission and role evaluation, trusted-origin matching (`$context.isTrustedOrigin`), IP extraction, error envelopes, API-key validation. The integration supplies only what better-auth leaves to the host: the mount, a faithful `Request`, a client IP, cookie write-back, refresh control where cookies cannot be written, and better-auth's origin rule on surfaces better-auth's router never sees.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          |

### 0.3 SOLID mapping

| Letter | Concrete design elements                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                         |
| ------ | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| **S**  | Each unit has one reason to change (§3.1):<br>• `MountCoordinator`: lifecycle timing.<br>• `AuthExchange`: `Request` construction, header hygiene, `auth.handler`, error conversion.<br>• `RequestScope`: the per-request ALS and state.<br>• `PrincipalResolver`: the source chain and memoization.<br>• `AuthorizationEvaluator`: requirement composition.<br>• `OriginCheck`: better-auth's origin and form-CSRF rules for cookie-carrying and cookie-setting operations.<br>• `TrustedOrigins`: the post-init trusted-origin set.<br>• `ErrorRedactor`: credential-free error causes.<br>• `HookBinder`: discovery into the plugin registry.<br>• `BootValidator`: fail-fast checks and advice collection.<br>• `BetterAuthGuard`: orchestration only; it holds no policy logic, no transport branch and no better-auth call of its own.<br>Platforms only translate I/O; transports only extract context and map errors.    |
| **O**  | Five extension points, each added by a new class, value or package, never by editing core (§4):<br>• `HttpPlatform`, selected by its own `supports()`;<br>• `AuthTransport`, selected by its own `handles()`;<br>• `PrincipalSource`, an ordered chain filtered by the kinds each route accepts;<br>• `AuthorizationPolicy`, carried by reference inside requirement metadata, so there is no registry to edit;<br>• hook methods, discovered.<br>Every extension contract has an optional `advise()` member, so a unit contributes its own boot hints without core knowing about it `[R1:NEST-r1-07]`. Param decorators for principal kinds and per-invocation values are built with public factories (`definePrincipalParam`, `defineInvocationParam`). Core contains no `switch`/`if` on platform, transport, principal-kind or policy names, and names none of them in messages. An architecture test enforces this (§14.7). |
| **L**  | Every contract lists its invariants: exact bytes, every `Set-Cookie`, a stable memo key per logical request, decisions per invocation, "denials are values, exceptions are infrastructure", delegated principals never widened, and more. Runner-agnostic conformance kits check them, and the built-in units and any third-party unit must pass the same kits (§14.1). Principals form a discriminated union, so policies narrow instead of casting.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            |
| **I**  | Contracts are small, and optional members add progressive disclosure:<br>• `HttpPlatform` separates lifecycle (`prepare`/`mount`) from per-request access (`HttpRequestAccessor`), so GraphQL-over-HTTP uses the accessor without mounting anything.<br>• `CookieSink` has one method.<br>• `AuthorizationPolicy` needs only `id` and `evaluate`.<br>• `PrincipalSource` needs only `id`, `kinds` and `resolve`.<br>• A transport without a browser leg (RPC) simply omits `TransportCall.browser`.<br>• Policies see an `AuthorizationContext`, never an `ExecutionContext` unless they ask for it.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                             |
| **D**  | Core depends on `AuthLike`, its own contracts and `Symbol.for` tokens. It reaches the plugin through a versioned protocol object found with `$context.getPlugin(id)`, never through an import. The principal resolver and the policy invoker sit behind tokens (`PRINCIPAL_RESOLVER`, `POLICY_INVOKER`) so tests can substitute them `[R2:NEST-r2-15]`. Platform and transport units depend on the contracts and their own peer framework, never on each other.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  |

### 0.4 What this design optimizes for and what it costs

- **Optimizes for:**
  - zero reimplementation of better-auth;
  - identical behavior across platforms, proven by kits rather than asserted;
  - third-party extension without forking;
  - fail-fast configuration, including every surface the guard cannot reach;
  - zero generics in the common case.
- **Costs** (accepted in §16):
  - one line in `auth.ts` (`nestjs()`);
  - one platform import in `forRoot` (`platforms: [expressPlatform()]`);
  - `@UseBetterAuth()` on every WebSocket gateway, on both Nest majors (§9.3);
  - an `Origin` header on unsafe requests that carry a cookie, from non-browser clients (SSR servers) and from cross-origin clients that also send a token, exactly as better-auth already requires on its own routes (§7.10);
  - a boot-time metadata scan;
  - a small hook-dispatch mirror kept in parity with `BA/api/dispatch.ts` and `BA/db/with-hooks.ts` by a property test.

| S6  | `isAPIError`, never `instanceof`; infrastructure → 5xx                                                                                                                      | §7.7, §8.1 (a 401 escaping a policy is re-classified by an authoritative re-resolution), §8.3.1 (API-key result mapping; outage probe with a read and a no-op write), §13 (taxonomy, normalization, redaction); ADR-13, ADR-16, ADR-42, ADR-43, ADR-59                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                   | better-auth's `getSessionFromCtx` swallows storage errors into 401 (LEAD-V36); the kernel does not pass that 401 on as a denial                                                                                                                 |
| S7  | Lazy principal resolution, at most once per request                                                                                                                         | §7.2 (memo scopes: request key, optional connection; the source set keyed by content; decisions per invocation; promise stored before settling; GraphQL root fields share the principal, never a decision); ADR-10, ADR-37                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                               | Services never start a resolution; they read the guard's (ADR-57)                                                                                                                                                                               |

---

## 2. Package layout and public API

One npm package, `nestjs-slightly-better-auth`. Every framework integration and every better-auth plugin integration lives in its own subpath. Optional peers are therefore imported statically, and only by the subpath that needs them. There is no `loadPackage`, no `createRequire` of peers and no top-level await (R:packaging §6; R:nest-di §8).

### 2.1 Entry points

| Subpath                 | Units                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              | Runtime imports                                                                                                                                                                          | Peers (§2.4)                                                               |
| ----------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `.`                     | Kernel: `BetterAuthModule`, guard, scope interceptor, service, decorators, tokens, contracts (SPI types), errors, type helpers, `betterAuthCorsOrigin()`. Built-in units re-exported by the composition root: `httpTransport()`; the session unit (`sessionPrincipal()`, `CurrentSession()`, `CurrentUser()`, `freshSession()`, `RequireFreshSession()`, `SESSION_PRINCIPAL_KIND`) | `@nestjs/common`, `@nestjs/core`, `better-auth/api`, `rxjs`                                                                                                                              | required only                                                              |
| `./plugin`              | `nestjs()` better-auth plugin                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      | `better-auth/api`, `better-auth/cookies`, `defu`                                                                                                                                         | `better-auth` only; **never** `@nestjs/*` or `node:*` (CI-enforced, §12.7) |
| `./platform`            | Helpers for Node-based third-party platforms and transports (header conversion, bounded body reader, Node response writer, absolute URL of an upgrade request)                                                                                                                                                                                                                     | Node built-ins                                                                                                                                                                           | none                                                                       |
| `./express`             | `expressPlatform()`, `ExpressPlatform`                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                             | none (structural types; drives the Nest adapter)                                                                                                                                         | none                                                                       |
| `./fastify`             | `fastifyPlatform()`, `FastifyPlatform`                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                             | none (structural types)                                                                                                                                                                  | none                                                                       |
| `./graphql`             | `apolloTransport()`, `mercuriusTransport()`, `mercuriusSubscriptionContext()`, `BetterAuthGraphqlDenial`, `BetterAuthGraphqlInternalError`                                                                                                                                                                                                                                         | `@nestjs/graphql`                                                                                                                                                                        | `@nestjs/graphql`, `graphql`                                               |
| `./websockets`          | `socketIoTransport()`, `wsTransport()`, `withUpgradeRequest()`, `recordUpgradeRequest()`, `WsConnectionAuth`, `WS_CONNECTION_AUTH`, `wsCloseCodeFor()`                                                                                                                                                                                                                             | `@nestjs/websockets`                                                                                                                                                                     | `@nestjs/websockets`                                                       |
| `./microservices`       | `rpcTransport()`, RPC credential carriers                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          | `@nestjs/microservices`                                                                                                                                                                  | `@nestjs/microservices`                                                    |
| `./admin`               | `permission()`, `RequirePermission()` (admin plugin)                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                               | core only                                                                                                                                                                                | admin plugin enabled (boot-checked)                                        |
| `./organization`        | `orgPermission()`, `RequireOrgPermission()`, `orgMember()`, `RequireOrgMember()`, organization refs (`activeOrganization()`, `fromParam()`, `fromHeader()`, `organizationRef()`), `ActiveOrganizationId()`, `ActiveMemberRole()`                                                                                                                                                   | core only                                                                                                                                                                                | organization plugin enabled (boot-checked)                                 |
| `./api-key`             | `apiKeyPrincipal()`, `apiKeyPermission()`, `RequireApiKeyPermission()`, `API_KEY_PRINCIPAL_KIND`                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                   | `better-auth/plugins/access`                                                                                                                                                             | `@better-auth/api-key` plugin enabled (boot-checked)                       |
| `./testing`             | Consumer test helpers                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              | `@nestjs/testing` (types), `better-auth`                                                                                                                                                 | `@nestjs/testing`                                                          |
| `./testing/conformance` | Runner-agnostic conformance kits for platforms, transports, principal sources, policies                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            | `@nestjs/core`, `@nestjs/testing`, `node:assert`; `better-auth`, `better-auth/api`, `better-auth/plugins`, `better-auth/adapters/memory` (the kits build their own real instance, §14.1) | `@nestjs/testing`                                                          |

Express and Fastify are separate subpaths even though they import no peer (ADR-05). They are extension units, and registering them explicitly is the same act a third party performs. Keeping them out of the root also lets the architecture test prove that core never depends on them. The session unit and `httpTransport()` are extension units too (they live in `src/extensions/**`); the root entry re-exports them because every app needs them.

### 2.2 Exported symbols with signatures

Types derived from the user's instance are always computed from `typeof auth`, never re-declared (§11). Signatures are normative; bodies are illustrative.

#### 2.2.1 `nestjs-slightly-better-auth`: module and options

```ts
import type {
  DynamicModule,
  InjectionToken,
  ModuleMetadata,
  OptionalFactoryDependency,
  Provider,
  Type,
} from "@nestjs/common";

export declare class BetterAuthModule {
  /** Default instance. Carries the app-level platforms and transports. When a Register augmentation exists, `auth` must be the registered type. */
  static forRoot<A extends AuthLike = RegisteredAuth>(
    options: BetterAuthModuleOptions<A> &
      BetterAuthAppOptions & { name?: "default" } & DefaultInstanceCheck<A>,
  ): DynamicModule;
  /** Named instance (§5.5): any better-auth instance. Platforms and transports are app-level and belong to the default instance. */
  static forRoot<A extends AuthLike>(
    options: BetterAuthModuleOptions<A> & { name: string } & NoAppOptions,
  ): DynamicModule;
  static forRootAsync<A extends AuthLike = RegisteredAuth>(
    options: BetterAuthModuleAsyncOptions<A> &
      BetterAuthAppOptions & { name?: "default" },
  ): DynamicModule;
  static forRootAsync<A extends AuthLike>(
    options: BetterAuthModuleAsyncOptions<A> & { name: string } & NoAppOptions,
  ): DynamicModule;
}

/**
 * App-level static options. An app has one HTTP adapter and one transport registry, so these are declared once,
 * on the default instance (type-level here; runtime check B25). [R1:NEST-r1-09]
 */
export interface BetterAuthAppOptions {
  /** HTTP platforms. Exactly one must support the running HTTP adapter when the app has one. Default []. */
  platforms?: readonly ExtensionRef<HttpPlatform>[];
  /** Transports, consulted in order BEFORE the built-in httpTransport(). Default []. */
  transports?: readonly ExtensionRef<AuthTransport>[];
}
type NoAppOptions = { readonly platforms?: never; readonly transports?: never };

/** Instance-shape options: they decide which providers exist, so they are fixed at definition time. [A][B][C] */
export interface BetterAuthStaticOptions {
  /** Instance name. Default 'default'. Named instances get their own tokens and mount (§5.5). */
  name?: string;
  /** Register the module as global. Default true. */
  isGlobal?: boolean;
  /**
   * Register BetterAuthGuard as APP_GUARD and BetterAuthScopeInterceptor as APP_INTERCEPTOR (both via useExisting).
   * Default true for the default instance, false for named instances.
   */
  globalGuard?: boolean;
  /** Principal sources of this instance, tried in order BEFORE the built-in session source, filtered per route by the kinds it accepts (§7.6). Default []. */
  principals?: readonly ExtensionRef<PrincipalSource>[];
}

/** Runtime options: read by providers after DI resolution, so they may come from useFactory. */
export type BetterAuthRuntimeOptions<A extends AuthLike = RegisteredAuth> = {
  /** The object returned by betterAuth(). Never wrapped, cloned or mutated. */
  auth: A;
  /** Access for handlers without an access decorator, unless a transport supplies the default (field resolvers inherit, §7.6). Default 'authenticated'. [C] */
  defaultAccess?: "authenticated" | "public";
  /**
   * Requirements every 'required' plan of this instance carries, ahead of its class and method requirements: a company-wide
   * rule such as orgMember(). Compiled into the plan, so boot validation, coverage, the guard and the decorators see one plan.
   * Replaces v2's protected BetterAuthGuard.planFor seam (§7.6). Default []. [R2:NEST-r2-08]
   */
  defaultRequirements?: readonly RequirementExpr[];
  /** HTTP mount options for this instance. */
  http?: HttpMountOptions;
  /** Set-Cookie forwarding for application-level direct auth.api calls (§7.5). [R1:BA-r1-02] */
  cookies?: CookieForwardingOptions;
  /** better-auth's origin rule on cookie-carrying app operations, and its form-CSRF rule on handlers that forward auth cookies (§7.10). [R1:SEC-r1-01] */
  originCheck?: OriginCheckOptions;
  /** Per-instance override of transport error objects for this instance's plans, and error logging (§13.5). */
  errors?: ErrorMappingOptions;
  /** Log the one-line boot summary. Default true. */
  logSummary?: boolean;
} & SessionOption<A>;

export interface CookieForwardingOptions {
  /**
   * Forward Set-Cookie produced by direct auth.api.* calls that application code makes inside a handler, when the call
   * carries the caller's own credential or none. Default false, which is better-auth's server-call semantics
   * (a server call never touches the browser unless you ask). Per handler: @ForwardAuthCookies(); per call site:
   * BetterAuthService.forwardCookies(fn). The library's own calls (principal sources and policies) always forward. Handlers with
   * forwarding on get better-auth's form-CSRF origin rule on unsafe operations (§7.10), so turning this on instance-wide applies it everywhere.
   */
  forwardDirectCalls?: boolean;
}

export interface OriginCheckOptions {
  /**
   * 'cookie' (default): an unsafe operation whose browser leg carries a cookie must come from a trusted origin, whatever credential
   * authenticated it, exactly as on better-auth's routes (§7.10). 'off': disabled (B19 warns in production). [R2:SEC-r2-01]
   */
  mode?: "cookie" | "off";
  /**
   * A cookie-authenticated unsafe operation without Origin or Referer.
   * 'reject' (default): 403 MISSING_OR_NULL_ORIGIN, exactly as better-auth's own routes answer (LEAD-V16).
   * 'allow-non-browser': allowed when Origin, Referer and Sec-Fetch-Site are all absent (no browser sends such a request cross-site). See §17 Q15.
   */
  missingOrigin?: "reject" | "allow-non-browser";
}

/** `session` is REQUIRED (with userId) when the session shape lacks user.id, i.e. customSession (§11.5). [C] */
export type SessionOption<A extends AuthLike> =
  HasUserId<SessionOf<A>> extends true
    ? { session?: SessionPrincipalOptions<SessionOf<A>> | false }
    : {
        session:
          | (SessionPrincipalOptions<SessionOf<A>> & {
              userId: (s: SessionOf<A>) => string | null;
            })
          | false;
      };

export interface SessionPrincipalOptions<S> {
  /** Map a (possibly customSession-shaped) session to its user id. Default s => s.user?.id ?? null. */
  userId?: (session: S) => string | null;
  /** Default freshness of identity reads; per route: @RequireAuth({ authoritative: true }). Default 'default'. */
  freshness?: "default" | "authoritative";
  /**
   * Does any apiKey() configuration of this instance set enableSessionForAPIKeys? The api-key plugin object does not expose
   * its configuration, so no unit can read it (§8.3.1). Unset (default): when the api-key plugin is present, the session
   * unit's boot advice W_API_KEY_FULL_SESSION / W_API_KEY_SESSION_MULTIPLIER is worded conditionally. false: you assert
   * that none does, and the advice is dropped. true: the advice is worded as a fact. [R1:BA-r1-05]
   */
  apiKeySessions?: boolean;
}

export interface HttpMountOptions {
  /** Mount better-auth routes on the platform. Default true. false = guard-only service. */
  mount?: boolean;
  /** Maximum auth-route request body. Default 1_048_576 (1 MiB). 413 above. */
  bodyLimit?: number | `${number}${"b" | "kb" | "mb"}`;
  /** Wrap every auth-route exchange (ORM request context, tracing). Outermost first. [A][C] */
  around?: readonly AuthHandlerInterceptor[];
  /** Allow a mount path of '/'. Default false (a root mount captures every unmatched route). [A] */
  allowRootMount?: boolean;
  /**
   * Allow an unset baseURL in production. better-auth then derives the base URL, token links and a trusted origin from
   * each request's Host header. Default false: boot fails with UNSAFE_BASE_URL (B23). [R1:SEC-r1-07]
   */
  allowRequestDerivedBaseURL?: boolean;
  /** Log each auth path better-auth answers 404 for once, with a "did you mean" (capped at 100 paths). Default: true outside production. [R1:SEC-r1-16] */
  diagnostics?: boolean;
}

export type AuthHandlerInterceptor = (
  call: {
    readonly request: Request;
    readonly platformRequest: unknown;
    readonly instance: string;
  },
  next: (request?: Request) => Promise<Response>,
) => Promise<Response>;

export type BetterAuthModuleOptions<A extends AuthLike> =
  BetterAuthStaticOptions & BetterAuthRuntimeOptions<A>;

export interface BetterAuthModuleAsyncOptions<
  A extends AuthLike,
> extends BetterAuthStaticOptions {
  imports?: ModuleMetadata["imports"];
  inject?: readonly (InjectionToken | OptionalFactoryDependency)[];
  useFactory: (
    ...args: any[]
  ) => BetterAuthFactoryResult<A> | Promise<BetterAuthFactoryResult<A>>;
}

/** A static or app-level key returned from useFactory is a compile error with a readable message (EXP-C9). [C] */
export type BetterAuthFactoryResult<A extends AuthLike> =
  BetterAuthRuntimeOptions<A> & {
    [
      K in keyof (BetterAuthStaticOptions & BetterAuthAppOptions)
    ]?: StaticOptionMustBePassedToForRootAsync<K>;
  };
export interface StaticOptionMustBePassedToForRootAsync<K extends string> {
  readonly __error: `'${K}' is a static option: pass it to forRootAsync() next to useFactory, not in its result`;
}
/** Rejects a different instance than the registered one for the default instance (EXP-C2). [C] */
export type DefaultInstanceCheck<A> = IsRegistered extends true
  ? A extends RegisteredAuth
    ? unknown
    : { auth: RegisteredAuth }
  : unknown;

// ── Extension registration (§4) [A][B] ────────────────────────────────────
/** A class (DI-constructed), a ready instance, or a definition that brings its own providers. */
export type ExtensionRef<T> = Type<T> | T | ExtensionDefinition<T>;
export interface ExtensionDefinition<T> {
  readonly [EXTENSION_DEFINITION]: true; // Symbol.for brand, set by defineExtension
  readonly use:
    | { readonly useClass: Type<T> }
    | {
        readonly useFactory: (...deps: any[]) => T | Promise<T>;
        readonly inject?: readonly InjectionToken[];
      }
    | { readonly useExisting: InjectionToken<T> };
  readonly providers?: readonly Provider[]; // e.g. the extension's own options provider
  readonly imports?: ModuleMetadata["imports"];
  /** Tokens (from `providers`) the forRoot module re-exports, globally when isGlobal: helper services for users. [R1:NEST-r1-12] */
  readonly exports?: readonly InjectionToken[];
}
export declare const EXTENSION_DEFINITION: unique symbol; // Symbol.for('nestjs-slightly-better-auth:extension')
export declare function defineExtension<T>(
  definition: Omit<ExtensionDefinition<T>, typeof EXTENSION_DEFINITION>,
): ExtensionDefinition<T>;
```

#### 2.2.2 Enhancers, service, resolver token

```ts
/**
 * Transport-neutral authentication + authorization (§7, §8). Singleton. It has no subclass seam: company-wide requirements are the
 * declarative `defaultRequirements` option, which every reader of a plan sees (§7.6). [R2:NEST-r2-08]
 */
export declare class BetterAuthGuard implements CanActivate {
  canActivate(context: ExecutionContext): Promise<boolean>;
}
/** Compiled once per (controller class, handler), never per handler alone (§7.6). [R2:NEST-r2-01] */
export interface RoutePlan {
  readonly instance: string;
  /**
   * 'inherit': a handler a transport declares as reached only through an already authorized operation (GraphQL field resolvers
   * without their own or class-level access, acceptance or requirement metadata, §9.2). The guard returns true with no I/O. [R2:NEST-r2-04]
   */
  readonly access: "public" | "optional" | "required" | "inherit";
  /** defaultRequirements first, then class requirements (base first), then method requirements; empty unless access is 'required'. */
  readonly requirements: readonly RequirementExpr[];
  /** 'authoritative' when the route asks for it, session.freshness says so, or a requirement demands fresh identity. */
  readonly freshness: "default" | "authoritative";
  /** Principal kinds admitted on the route (§7.6): @AcceptPrincipals or the instance's default kinds, plus kinds requirements name. */
  readonly accepts: ReadonlySet<string>;
  /** Kind constraints contributed by param decorators (e.g. @CurrentSession() → { kind: 'session', reason: 'SESSION_REQUIRED' }); checked at boot (B15). */
  readonly principalParams: readonly {
    readonly kind: string;
    readonly reason: string;
  }[];
  /**
   * The origin check (§7.10). 'cookie': better-auth's rule when the browser leg carries a cookie. 'form': better-auth's
   * form-CSRF rule, which also covers requests without a cookie (handlers with @ForwardAuthCookies(), such as login proxies).
   * 'off': @SkipOriginCheck() or originCheck.mode 'off'. [R2:SEC-r2-08]
   */
  readonly originCheck: "cookie" | "form" | "off";
  /** Content key of the sources this plan consults (ordered source indexes, interned per instance); part of the principal memo key (§7.2). [R2:NEST-r2-16] */
  readonly sourceSet: string;
  /** Set-Cookie of application direct calls is forwarded (§7.5). */
  readonly forwardDirectCalls: boolean;
  readonly site: string; // 'ProjectsController.remove'
  /** Names of `:params` in the Nest route path (HTTP controllers; read from Nest's path metadata), for boot advice. */
  readonly routeParams: readonly string[];
}

/** Opens the per-invocation scope used by the cookie bridge, refresh suppression, param decorators and the service. */
export declare class BetterAuthScopeInterceptor implements NestInterceptor {
  intercept(context: ExecutionContext, next: CallHandler): Observable<unknown>;
}

/**
 * Applies BetterAuthGuard + BetterAuthScopeInterceptor explicitly (every gateway, hybrid RPC controllers, globalGuard: false).
 * Handlers a transport claims as reachable only explicitly need both enhancers; B16 names this decorator (§5.4). [R2:NEST-r2-11]
 */
export declare function UseBetterAuth(): ClassDecorator & MethodDecorator;

export declare class BetterAuthService<A extends AuthLike = RegisteredAuth> {
  readonly name: string;
  /** The better-auth instance, unchanged and fully typed. */
  readonly instance: A;
  /** instance.api: plain better-auth server calls (§7.5: forwarding is opt-in; refresh is suppressed in cookie-less scopes). */
  readonly api: A["api"];
  /** Memoized await of instance.$context (resolves immediately after boot). */
  context(): Promise<Awaited<A["$context"]>>;
  /** Mount information after bootstrap; undefined when not mounted. */
  mount():
    | {
        readonly basePath: string;
        readonly bodyLimit: number;
        readonly platform: string;
      }
    | undefined;
  /**
   * Principal of the current handler scope: the result the guard produced for this invocation. It never starts a resolution
   * (no better-auth I/O), so a public handler gets null (§7.6), and a handler whose guard did not run throws NO_AUTH_RESULT.
   * Outside any handler scope (guards, middleware, policies, background jobs) it throws a request-time configuration error
   * NO_AUTH_SCOPE: that is never mistaken for "anonymous". [R2:NEST-r2-07, SEC-r2-04]
   */
  getPrincipal(): Promise<AuthPrincipal | null>;
  /** The `session` field of the current principal when it carries one (session principals), else null. Same scope rules as getPrincipal(). */
  getSession(): Promise<SessionOf<A> | null>;
  /**
   * Synchronous reader for guards and interceptors that run after BetterAuthGuard: the result the guard produced for this
   * execution context and this instance, or undefined when the guard has not resolved one (or the plan belongs to another instance).
   * Never performs I/O. Lookup: the plan's principal memo entry (peek), then the invocation and carrier stamps, then a test stamp. [R2:NEST-r2-07]
   */
  principalFor(context: ExecutionContext): PrincipalResult | undefined;
  /** Web Headers for a direct auth.api call from a platform request: pseudo-headers dropped, client-IP header set. [A] */
  headersFrom(platformRequest: unknown): Headers;
  /**
   * Run fn with Set-Cookie forwarding enabled for direct calls inside it (§7.5). By default only calls that carry the
   * caller's own credential or none are forwarded; anyCredential: true forwards every call (deliberate account switching).
   */
  forwardCookies<T>(
    fn: () => Promise<T>,
    options?: { anyCredential?: boolean },
  ): Promise<T>;
  /** Run fn in a cookie-less scope: every auth.api call inside has session refresh suppressed (§7.4). [C] */
  withoutCookies<T>(fn: () => Promise<T>): Promise<T>;
  /** Run fn outside the current scope: no forwarding, no suppression (plain better-auth). [C] */
  runOutsideScope<T>(fn: () => Promise<T>): Promise<T>;
}

/** The resolver port the guard, decorators and service use. Default: ChainPrincipalResolver. [B] */
export interface PrincipalResolver {
  resolve(
    call: TransportCall,
    request: ResolutionRequest,
  ): Promise<PrincipalResult>;
  /** Settled result for this call and request if the guard already resolved it; never performs I/O. */
  peek(
    call: TransportCall,
    request: ResolutionRequest,
  ): PrincipalResult | undefined;
}
export interface ResolutionRequest {
  readonly auth: AuthHandle;
  readonly freshness: "default" | "authoritative";
  /** Kinds the route accepts; sources producing none of them are not consulted (§7.6). */
  readonly accepts: ReadonlySet<string>;
  /** The plan's content key of those sources (RoutePlan.sourceSet). */
  readonly sourceSet: string;
  /** Resolve again without reading or writing the memo: the re-classification of a 401 a policy call met (§8.1). [R2:BA-r2-03] */
  readonly bypassMemo?: boolean;
}

/** The port the evaluator calls a policy through. Default: policy.evaluate(params, context). Tests substitute it (overrideDecisions, §14.8). [R2:NEST-r2-15] */
export interface PolicyInvoker {
  invoke<P>(
    policy: AuthorizationPolicy<P, any>,
    params: P,
    context: AuthorizationContext,
  ): Promise<AuthorizationDecision>;
}
```

#### 2.2.3 Decorators

```ts
// Access (class or method; method overrides class; §7.6) [A][B][C]
export declare function Public(): ClassDecorator & MethodDecorator; // zero auth I/O
export declare function OptionalAuth(): ClassDecorator & MethodDecorator; // resolve if present; anonymous allowed
export declare function RequireAuth(options?: {
  authoritative?: boolean;
}): ClassDecorator & MethodDecorator;
export declare function UseAuthInstance(
  name: string,
): ClassDecorator & MethodDecorator; // named instance (§5.5)
/** Principal kinds admitted on the route; replaces the instance's default kinds (method overrides class). [R1:SEC-r1-02] */
export declare function AcceptPrincipals(
  ...kinds: readonly [PrincipalKind, ...PrincipalKind[]]
): ClassDecorator & MethodDecorator;

// Cookies and origin (§7.5, §7.10)
/**
 * Forward Set-Cookie of this handler's direct auth.api calls (same credential or none). Default: cookies.forwardDirectCalls.
 * Because such a handler can sign a browser in, its unsafe operations get better-auth's form-CSRF rule (origin check mode 'form',
 * §7.10), also on @Public() routes and without a cookie, as better-auth's own sign-in routes do. That check runs in the guard, so
 * B16 counts forwarding as declaring something and does not treat such a @Public() as coverage: under globalGuard: false the
 * handler needs @UseBetterAuth() (§5.4). [R1:BA-r1-02] [R2:SEC-r2-08]
 */
export declare function ForwardAuthCookies(
  enabled?: boolean,
): ClassDecorator & MethodDecorator;
/** Exempt this route from the origin check (e.g. a server-to-server endpoint that receives forwarded cookies). [R1:SEC-r1-01] */
export declare function SkipOriginCheck(): ClassDecorator & MethodDecorator;

// Authorization (§8) [B][C]
export declare function Require(
  ...requirements: readonly RequirementExpr[]
): ClassDecorator & MethodDecorator; // AND
export declare function anyOf(
  ...requirements: readonly RequirementExpr[]
): RequirementExpr;
export declare function allOf(
  ...requirements: readonly RequirementExpr[]
): RequirementExpr;
export declare function requirement<P>(
  policy: PolicyRef<P>,
  params: P,
  options?: RequirementOptions,
): Requirement<P>;
export interface RequirementOptions {
  readonly label?: string;
  /** Overrides policy.requires.principals for this requirement. */
  readonly principals?: readonly PrincipalKind[];
  /** Overrides policy.requires.freshIdentity for this requirement. */
  readonly freshIdentity?: boolean;
}

// Parameters (synchronous; all transports; §7.8) [A][C]. They read the handler plan's instance (@UseAuthInstance): v2's
// `instance` option could only repeat the plan's instance or name one the guard never resolved. [R2:NEST-r2-14]
export declare function CurrentSession(): ParameterDecorator; // AuthSession; kind 'session' (B15 PRINCIPAL_PARAM_CONFLICT when the route admits another kind) [R1:NEST-r1-10]
export declare function CurrentUser(): ParameterDecorator; // AuthUser; kind 'session'
export declare function CurrentPrincipal(): ParameterDecorator; // AuthPrincipal | null; any kind
/** Factory for kind-constrained principal params; @CurrentSession() is built with it. Core stores the kind as data. [R1:NEST-r1-07] */
export declare function definePrincipalParam<K extends PrincipalKind, R>(spec: {
  readonly kind: K;
  readonly reason: string; // reported by B15 when the route admits another kind
  readonly project: (principal: PrincipalOfKind<K>) => R;
}): () => ParameterDecorator;
/**
 * Factory for params that return a value a policy published for this invocation (AuthorizationContext.provide). `missing` is the
 * `detail` of the request-time configuration error thrown when nothing was published: logged, never sent to clients (§7.8). [R1:SEC-r1-19]
 */
export declare function defineInvocationParam(
  slot: symbol,
  spec: { readonly missing: string },
```

#### 2.2.6 Errors (§13)

```ts
export type AuthErrorCode = "UNAUTHENTICATED" | "FORBIDDEN" | "RATE_LIMITED";
/** Transport-neutral denial value. Only transports turn it into something throwable. [B][C] */
export interface AuthFailure {
  readonly status: 401 | 403 | 429;
  readonly code: AuthErrorCode;
  readonly reason?: string; // better-auth body.code or a policy/library reason
  readonly message: string;
  readonly challenge?: string; // WWW-Authenticate value
  readonly headers?: Headers; // e.g. Retry-After; set-cookie cleanup is forwarded separately
}
export declare const AuthFailures: {
  unauthenticated(message?: string): AuthFailure; // 401 UNAUTHENTICATED
  rejected(input: {
    status: 401 | 403 | 429;
    reason?: string;
    message?: string;
    challenge?: string;
    retryAfterSeconds?: number;
  }): AuthFailure;
  forbidden(reason: string, message?: string): AuthFailure; // 403 FORBIDDEN
  /** 401/403/429 APIError → failure (Retry-After from its headers or body.details.tryAgainIn ms); else null. */
  fromAPIError(error: unknown): AuthFailure | null;
};
export declare function isAuthFailure(value: unknown): value is AuthFailure; // Symbol.for brand
/**
 * Thrown at boot (aggregated) and at request time for misconfiguration only (surfaces as 500). Boot errors carry the detail in
 * `message`: they never reach a client. Request-time errors are created with `atRequest`, whoever throws them (guard, param
 * decorator, service, source, normalizeThrown), so they are safe even where no transport maps them. [R1:SEC-r1-19]
 */
export declare class BetterAuthConfigurationError extends Error {
  constructor(code: string, detail: string, hint?: string);
  /**
   * A request-time configuration error: `message` is the fixed 'Authentication is misconfigured'; `detail`, `site` and `hint`
   * are ordinary own properties, which Nest's logger prints (LEAD-V31) and GraphQL drivers do not send (LEAD-EXP-7).
   */
  static atRequest(
    code: string,
    detail: string,
    options?: { site?: string; hint?: string },
  ): BetterAuthConfigurationError;
  readonly code: string;
  readonly detail: string; // boot: equals message; request time: never in message
  readonly site?: string; // e.g. 'SiteResolver.me'
  readonly hint?: string;
  readonly phase: "boot" | "request";
  /** Copied into GraphQL errors by both drivers when the error is thrown where no transport maps it (graphql-js originalError.extensions). */
  readonly extensions: {
    readonly code: "INTERNAL_SERVER_ERROR";
    readonly reason: "AUTH_MISCONFIGURED";
    readonly statusCode: 500;
  };
  readonly issues?: readonly BetterAuthConfigurationError[]; // set on the aggregated boot error
}
/**
 * Wraps an infrastructure fault (DB down, APIError >= 500, unknown error). Never 401/403. Not intrinsic: Nest logs it.
 * Generic, detail-free message ("Authentication service unavailable"). Transports that map it send their own generic text instead
 * (§13.3); only where nothing maps it (thrown outside the guard in a GraphQL resolver body) does a driver copy this message. `cause` is a REDACTED Error: name, code/errno and
 * the first line of the original message with every credential value of the request removed (§13.4). [R1:SEC-r1-08]
 */
export declare class BetterAuthInfrastructureError extends Error {
  constructor(cause: unknown, options?: { secrets?: readonly string[] });
  readonly cause: Error;
  readonly extensions: {
    readonly code: "INTERNAL_SERVER_ERROR";
    readonly reason: "AUTH_UNAVAILABLE";
  };
}
/** The unredacted cause, only when errors.exposeRawCause is true; otherwise undefined. Kept under a non-enumerable Symbol.for slot. */
export declare function getRawCause(
  error: BetterAuthInfrastructureError,
): unknown;
/** Symbol.for brand checks, safe across package copies. Library code never uses instanceof on its own classes (§12.5). [R1:SEC-r1-19] */
export declare function isInfrastructureError(
  value: unknown,
): value is BetterAuthInfrastructureError;
export declare function isConfigurationError(
  value: unknown,
): value is BetterAuthConfigurationError;
export type {
  AuthErrorBody,
  AuthGraphqlExtensions,
  AuthTransportErrorPayload,
  ErrorMappingOptions,
} from "./errors";
```

```ts
import type {
  IncomingHttpHeaders,
  IncomingMessage,
  ServerResponse,
} from "node:http";
/** Node headers → Web Headers: drops ':'-prefixed pseudo-headers and symbol keys, appends array values; sets host from :authority if absent. */
export declare function toWebHeaders(
  raw: IncomingHttpHeaders | Record<string | symbol, unknown>,
): Headers;
/** true if the request may carry a body (not GET/HEAD, and content-length > 0 or transfer-encoding present). */
export declare function mayHaveBody(
  method: string,
  headers: IncomingHttpHeaders,

/**
 * Read at most `limit` bytes. Never throws for size: resolves { ok: false, reason: 'too-large' } instead.
 * drainOnOverflow: keep consuming and discarding (up to drainCap, then destroy the socket) so later middleware sees a finished stream.
 */
export declare function readBoundedBody(
  stream: NodeJS.ReadableStream | ReadableStream<Uint8Array>,
  options: {
    limit: number;
    declaredLength?: number;
    drainOnOverflow?: boolean;
    drainCap?: number; // drain* apply to Node streams only
  },
): Promise<
  | { ok: true; bytes: Uint8Array }

export declare function bindAsyncContext<F extends (...args: any[]) => any>(
  fn: F,
): F;
/** Degraded tier (§6.4.3): req.rawBody if present, else re-serialize req.body for its content type (warns once). */
export declare function recoverConsumedBody(
  req: IncomingMessage & { body?: unknown; rawBody?: Buffer },
): Uint8Array | null;
/**
 * Absolute URL of a WebSocket upgrade or handshake request, for the browser leg of the origin check (§7.10): scheme from the
 * socket's TLS state, else the first X-Forwarded-Proto value; host from the first X-Forwarded-Host value, else Host; then the path.
 * Forwarded headers are acceptable here because a browser cannot set them on an upgrade, and the value only serves the origin
 * check of that browser's request. [R2:SEC-r2-05]
```

Default header allow-list for every carrier: `authorization`, `cookie`, `x-api-key`. RPC messages carry no `Host`, so `rpcTransport()` declares host-less server calls (`requires.hostlessCalls`, §5.4 B20) `[R2:BA-r2-05]`.

### 2.3 Tokens and metadata keys (S5) [A][B][C]

Every identity-sensitive value is copy-safe. If the CJS and ESM builds are both loaded, `Symbol.for` keys still match, so metadata written by one copy is visible to the other (R:packaging §5.2: `Symbol()` keys fail silently; `Symbol.for` works).

| Kind                         | Key (`Symbol.for('nestjs-slightly-better-auth:<…>')`)                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                         |
| ---------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| DI tokens                    | `instance:<name>`, `options:<name>`, `service:<name>`, `handle:<name>`, `principal-resolver`, `policy-invoker`, `transports`, `platforms`, `principal-sources:<name>`, `instance-registry`, `request-scope`, `mount-coordinator`, `ws-connection-auth`; `ext:<point>:<instance>:<i>` (one provider per extension list entry, §4 and §5.7: e.g. `ext:principals:<name>:<i>`, `ext:platforms:default:<i>`, `ext:transports:default:<i>`)                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        |
| Metadata keys (class/method) | `access`, `accept-principals`, `requirements`, `freshness`, `auth-instance`, `principal-params`, `invocation-params`, `forward-cookies`, `skip-origin-check`, `use-better-auth`, `hook`, `db-hook`                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            |
| Runtime brands and slots     | `bridge` (protocol object on the plugin), `extension` (ExtensionDefinition brand), `failure` (AuthFailure brand), `error` (brand on `BetterAuthInfrastructureError` and `BetterAuthConfigurationError`), `resolution` (principal results: the invocation's own result on the invocation object, and an operation-wide map by memo key on a carrier object, §7.8), `invocation` (per-invocation values on an invocation object), `raw-body` (Express capture), `upgrade-request` (ws), `mounted` (per-server double-mount stamp), `raw-cause` (non-enumerable slot on infrastructure errors), `test-app` (slot on the plugin handle used by `initTestApp`), `test-stamp` (`stampPrincipal()` record on an args array and its elements, §7.8). Extension units own further keys under the same prefix, for example `org:active-organization-id` and `org:active-member-role` (`./organization`) |

- Metadata is written with `SetMetadata`-style decorators under these keys. Requirement decorators **append** to the target's own array rather than overwriting it (§8.2).
- `Reflector.createDecorator` is not used. Its key is typed `string` and defaults to a random `uid(21)` per copy.
- `DiscoveryService.createDecorator` is not used. It allows one key per class, and its key is random (R:nest-di §3.1, §6.2).
- Library code never writes `req.session` or `req.user`, which express-session and Passport own.

- **Not peers:**
  - `@nestjs/platform-express`, `@nestjs/platform-fastify`, `express`, `fastify`, `@nestjs/apollo`, `@nestjs/mercurius`, `@nestjs/platform-ws`, `socket.io`: we never import them; platforms reach the server through `HttpAdapterHost` and structural types.
  - `better-call`: `APIError`/`isAPIError` come from `better-auth/api`.
  - `@better-auth/core`: not resolvable under pnpm's strict layout.
  - `@better-auth/api-key`: `./api-key` calls `auth.api.verifyApiKey` and never imports the package; its presence is boot-checked (B13).
  - `typescript`: TS 7 is npm `latest`, and a runtime library should not constrain it (R:packaging §9.12).

## 3. Architecture

### 3.1 Units

| #   | Unit                                                           | Purpose                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      | Interface                                                            | Depends on                                       |
| --- | -------------------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------ |
| U1  | `nestjs()` plugin (`./plugin`)                                 | The only code inside better-auth's pipeline: hook and DB-hook dispatchers, cookie bridge with credential matching, refresh suppression, client-IP header default, pre-bind counter for endpoint dispatches and database writes, a record of endpoint-produced results `[R2:BA-r2-06]`, protocol object                                                                       | `BetterAuthPlugin` + `BridgeHandle` (§10.2)                          | `better-auth/api`, `better-auth/cookies`, `defu` |
