| The library's own Responses (413 `PAYLOAD_TOO_LARGE`, 400 `INVALID_REQUEST_URL`) | built by core as Web `Response`s and written through the same path, so they are byte-identical across platforms and carry host CORS headers (H4) `[R1:NEST-r1-04]`                                                                                                                                                                                 | EXP-B:E1/E4; LEAD-EXP-2                                                                                              |
| Failures                                                                         | never answered with a platform's default error body. A rejected `handle()` reaches the host error pipeline at request time: Express `next(err)`; Fastify's child error handler, which delegates to the root's current handler (H8, §6.4.2). With `onAPIError.throw` the original `APIError` travels the same way (H13) `[R1:NEST-r1-04, BA-r1-09]` | LEAD-EXP-2; LEAD-V25                                                                                                 |
| Nest interceptors, pipes and serializers                                         | never run on auth routes. Exception filters see auth routes only for those failures                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                | better-auth principles P1/P2 (§0.2)                                                                                  |

### 6.8 Client IP for rate limiting `[A][B][C]`

better-auth reads the client IP **only from headers**; the default is `x-forwarded-for`. With no usable IP in production, rate limiting falls back to one shared bucket per path, and sign-in is limited to 3 per 10 s for everyone (`CORE/utils/ip.ts:353-383`; `BA/api/rate-limiter/index.ts:342, 442-451`). A Web `Request` cannot carry the socket address, so the host must supply it. The design splits the job so that proxy trust is configured once, in the platform, for the whole app:

1. **The platform decides trust.** Express `req.ip` honors `app.set('trust proxy', …)`; Fastify `request.ip` honors `trustProxy`. Each platform accepts a `clientIp` override.
2. **The plugin declares the header.** `nestjs()` returns `{ options: { advanced: { ipAddress: { ipAddressHeaders: [header] } } } }` from `init()`. better-auth merges plugin options with `defu(userOptions, pluginOptions)` (LEAD-V4), so this is a construction-time _default_, not a mutation (S1). A user-configured list stays first and ours is appended. The merged options feed both the rate limiter and session IP recording (`db/internal-adapter.ts:501`).

   **Interaction with better-auth's own proxy trust** `[R2:BA-r2-04]`. When the user set no `ipAddressHeaders`, ours becomes the **only** header better-auth reads, so `X-Forwarded-For` is no longer consulted, and better-auth still applies `advanced.ipAddress.trustedProxies` to our header's value (`CORE/utils/ip.ts:311-331, 364-377`). With the platform's trust off behind a load balancer inside `trustedProxies`, the value is the balancer's address, which better-auth discards: every client resolves to no IP and shares one bucket (REV2-BA:`exp4-trustedproxies-header.mjs`: plain better-auth `203.0.113.7`, with the plugin `null`, with the platform's trust on `203.0.113.7`). With the platform's trust set, the value is the client's address and `trustedProxies` is harmless. A deployment configured the better-auth way therefore sets the platform's trust proxy when it adds `nestjs()`, or keeps better-auth's chain parsing with `nestjs({ clientIpHeader: false })`. B18 warns in production about exactly this combination.

3. **The header name is unguessable** `[R1:SEC-r1-18]`. By default `nestjs()` generates `x-nsba-ip-<32 hex chars>` once per `nestjs()` call with `globalThis.crypto.randomUUID()` (Web Crypto, so the plugin stays runtime-agnostic): one name per plugin instance, so an app with named instances (§5.5) has several. The name never leaves the process. A code path that forwards raw client headers to better-auth, such as a custom controller calling `auth.handler(new Request(url, { headers: req.headers }))` or `auth.api.signInEmail({ headers: fromNodeHeaders(req.headers) })`, therefore cannot be abused to pick a rate-limit bucket or a recorded IP. A fixed name is used only when `clientIpHeader` is set explicitly (for a trusted sidecar that calls `auth.handler` itself).
4. **Core strips and sets.** `AuthExchange` deletes any client-supplied copy of the header, and any `x-nsba-ip-*` header, then sets it from `inbound.clientIp`. For app routes the kernel does the same on `TransportCall.headers()` using `call.clientIp`, so direct `auth.api.signInEmail({ headers })` calls record the right IP. `BetterAuthService.headersFrom(req)` does it too. The name is read from the plugin's protocol object (`handle.clientIpHeader`), so the plugin is the single source of truth.
5. **Verified end to end** (with the v1 fixed name; the random name changes nothing on this path). EXP-A:`exp-e2e.mjs` covers Nest 11/12 × Express/Fastify; EXP-B:E9 and EXP-C7 ran with `NODE_ENV=production`:
   - better-auth sees the trust-proxy-resolved IP;
   - a spoofed header is ignored;
   - the third request from one IP gets 429 while another IP gets 200;
   - a user list is kept first: `["cf-connecting-ip", <our header>]`.
6. **Proxy-trust diagnostics** `[R1:SEC-r1-06]`. The two classic misconfigurations are silent. better-auth's own "shared bucket" warning fires only in the `trustedProxies` case of item 2, where the IP resolves to none; otherwise the platform always supplies a valid, wrong IP `[R2:BA-r2-04]`:
   - _trust off behind a proxy_: every client gets the proxy's IP (or, with better-auth's `trustedProxies` covering it, no IP), so one attacker sending 3 sign-ins every 10 s locks out every user;
   - _trust everything_: `req.ip` is the client-chosen left-most `X-Forwarded-For` value, so rotating it bypasses the limit.

   Platforms therefore report `proxyTrust()` (Express from `app.get('trust proxy')`, Fastify from `initialConfig.trustProxy`). The boot summary prints it. B27 warns when it is `'all'` in production. In production, the first auth-route request that carries `x-forwarded-for`, `forwarded` or `x-real-ip` while trust is `'none'` logs `W_PROXY_UNTRUSTED` once, naming the socket IP and what better-auth made of it (§6.3 step 7). Migration step 8 (§15.1) walks through the setting.

7. **Opt-out.** `nestjs({ clientIpHeader: false })`. The user then configures `advanced.ipAddress` themselves (better-auth's `trustedProxies` with `X-Forwarded-For`), and B18 warns in production if nothing is configured.

### 6.9 CORS, global prefix and versioning

**CORS stays with the host** `[A][B][C]`. better-auth emits no CORS headers and answers preflight with 404; `trustedOrigins` is its CSRF check, not CORS (R:ba-integrations §0.2). The library configures no CORS. Its job is to make sure host CORS reaches auth routes:

- **Express:** the dispatcher is registered after `enableCors()` and `app.use()`.
- **Fastify:** the auth route is a real Fastify route answered through `reply`, so `@fastify/cors` hooks and preflight apply, including on the canonical 413.

Preflight 204 with ACAO, and ACAO on 200, 302 and 413, were verified on both platforms and both majors (EXP-B:E1/E4, EXP-A:`exp-e2e`, EXP-C4/C6, LEAD-EXP-2). We never call `enableCors` ourselves: Fastify throws on double registration (#52) and Express would apply it app-wide (#69, #95).

**`betterAuthCorsOrigin(auth, { allowPatterns? })`** is a `cors` / `@fastify/cors` origin callback for teams that want CORS to follow better-auth's trusted origins `[C]` `[R1:BA-r1-11, SEC-r1-17]`:

- **The trusted set is the post-init one** (`TrustedOrigins`, U17). `(await auth.$context).trustedOrigins` is computed before plugins' `init()` run, and plugin-contributed origins (for example `expo()` adding `exp://` in development) live only in the post-init `ctx.options.trustedOrigins` (LEAD-V17). The helper therefore merges `ctx.trustedOrigins` with the post-init array. It matches through better-auth's own matcher, `ctx.isTrustedOrigin.call({ trustedOrigins: merged }, origin)`, which keeps better-auth's wildcard and custom-scheme semantics. The origin check (§7.10) uses the same resolver.
- **Exact origins only by default.** `trustedOrigins` exists for CSRF and redirect allow-listing. By default the helper allows an origin only if it equals a trusted entry that is an exact `http(s)` origin with no wildcard. Exact `http:` origins are kept because development uses `http://localhost:3000`. Wildcard and custom-scheme matches need `allowPatterns: true`. This default excludes **only** wildcard and custom-scheme entries: without it, every origin a pattern such as `https://*.vercel.app` (preview deployments) matches would gain credentialed read access wherever the helper applies.
- **Every exact trusted origin gains credentialed CORS wherever the helper applies.** The helper cannot tell why an origin is trusted. A partner origin listed exactly in `trustedOrigins` only so that it is accepted as a `callbackURL` is, to the helper, an allowed origin like any other, so it can read the responses of every route the helper covers with the user's cookies. That is why the helper belongs on the auth mount (next bullet) and app routes get their own allow-list.
- **Function-valued `trustedOrigins(request)`** cannot be evaluated without a request, and a CORS origin callback receives none, so the helper throws at first use with a hint to supply your own `origin` function `[C]`. That is safer than silently using init-time values.
- **Scope.** The docs recommend an explicit CORS allow-list for app routes, and show how to scope the helper to the auth mount: on Express `app.use(basePath, cors({ origin: betterAuthCorsOrigin(auth), credentials: true }))` when app routes need no CORS, or one `cors` middleware whose per-request options delegate picks the helper for paths under the mount and the allow-list elsewhere (§15.1 step 4); on Fastify an `@fastify/cors` `delegator` keyed on the request path. An app-wide `app.enableCors({ origin: betterAuthCorsOrigin(auth), credentials: true })` is documented only with the caveat of the previous bullet. Case `LIB-cors-helper` (§14.5) tests the helper.

**Global prefix and versioning** `[A][B][C]`. Auth routes live at better-auth's own path, outside `setGlobalPrefix` and `enableVersioning`, because raw platform routes are subject to neither (R:nest-platform §5).

- There is one source of truth: better-auth's client, OAuth callbacks and `trustedOrigins` all derive from `baseURL`/`basePath`.
- To serve auth under `/v1`, set better-auth's `basePath: '/v1/api/auth'` or put the path in `baseURL`.
- We read `ApplicationConfig.getGlobalPrefix()`, a public API, only for the boot summary. We never mutate `ApplicationConfig`, because a later `setGlobalPrefix(p, opts)` would overwrite it (R:nest-platform §2.5).
- This fixes the reference's `/api/api/auth` regressions (PR #80) by construction.

### 6.10 Error handling on auth routes

| Source                                                                                                        | Result                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  |
| ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| better-auth Response (any status, redirect, stream)                                                           | verbatim                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                |
| `APIError` thrown out of `auth.handler`, `onAPIError.throw` **unset** (init failure, disallowed dynamic host) | its Response: status, JSON body, `headers` + hidden `better-call:api-error-headers` (Set-Cookie appended)                                                                                                                                               |
| `APIError` thrown out of `auth.handler` with `onAPIError: { throw: true }`                                    | rethrown unchanged to the host error pipeline (Express `next(err)`, Fastify rejection → child error handler → Nest's handler) with its hidden headers, so the user's filters decide `[R1:BA-r1-09]`                                                     |
| Body over limit                                                                                               | `413 { code: 'PAYLOAD_TOO_LARGE', message }`, identical on every platform, after host middleware (Express flag) or through the Fastify scope's child error handler (§6.4.2)                                                                             |
| Unparsable URL                                                                                                | `400 { code: 'INVALID_REQUEST_URL', message }`                                                                                                                                                                                                          |
| Any other throw (init failure, disallowed dynamic host, adapter bug)                                          | `BetterAuthInfrastructureError` (redacted cause, §13.4) → host error pipeline (Express `next(err)`, Fastify rejection → child error handler) → Nest's global filters → 500, logged (R:nest-platform §4.5 exp 9; EXP-C5; LEAD-EXP-2). Never 401/403 (S6) |
| 404 from better-auth for a matched path                                                                       | verbatim (bodiless); one WARN per path with a "did you mean" when `http.diagnostics` is on (§6.3 step 7) `[R1:SEC-r1-16]`                                                                                                                               |
| Client disconnects mid-exchange                                                                               | `signal` aborts; the write is abandoned without error logs                                                                                                                                                                                              |

### 6.11 HTTP/2

Pseudo-headers and the HTTP/2 symbol key are dropped by `toWebHeaders`, and `host` is set from `:authority` when absent, so HTTP/2 does not crash the exchange. Fastify's `request.host` falls back to `:authority`. `FastifyPlatform` declares `capabilities.http2`, and the kit runs `H-h2-pseudo` against `new FastifyAdapter({ http2: true })`. Express has no HTTP/2 server in Nest.

## 7. Authentication (principal resolution)

Authentication answers "who is calling". It produces an `AuthPrincipal`, a discriminated union over the augmentable `PrincipalKinds`. Authorization (§8) answers "may they" and never re-resolves identity.

### 7.1 Guard flow `[A][B][C]` `[R2:NEST-r2-01, NEST-r2-03, NEST-r2-08, SEC-r2-01]`

```
BetterAuthGuard.canActivate(ctx)
 ├─ plan = planner.get(ctx.getClass(), ctx.getHandler())   // cached per (class, handler), never per handler alone (7.6); no transport needed
 ├─ if plan.access === 'inherit' → return true             // a field resolver inside an operation already authorized (9.2): no I/O
 ├─ if plan.access === 'public' && plan.originCheck !== 'form' → return true            // zero auth I/O, in any context type
 ├─ transport = transports.select(ctx)                      // first handles(ctx); none → BetterAuthConfigurationError NO_TRANSPORT (500), never allow
 ├─ kernel    = instances.get(plan.instance)
 ├─ call      = transport.describe(ctx, kit)                // sync, no I/O; headers lazy
 ├─ if plan.originCheck !== 'off' && call.browser?.enforce:                                            // 7.10, before any better-auth I/O
 │     failure = await kernel.handle.checkOrigin(call.browser, plan.originCheck)                        // one verdict per browser leg
 │     failure → throw transport.toException(failure, ctx)                                              // 403 INVALID_ORIGIN / MISSING_OR_NULL_ORIGIN / …
 ├─ if plan.access === 'public' → return true                                                           // a public login proxy after its form check
 ├─ result = await resolver.resolve(call, { auth: kernel.handle, freshness: plan.freshness, accepts: plan.accepts, sourceSet: plan.sourceSet })  // 7.2
 ├─ stamp(call, plan, result)                               // the invocation's own result; the carrier's entry under the plan's memo key (7.8)
 ├─ result.outcome === 'rejected' → throw transport.toException(result.failure, ctx)                   // never downgraded
 ├─ result.outcome === 'absent'   → plan.access === 'optional' ? return true
 │                                                                : throw toException(AuthFailures.unauthenticated())
 ├─ !plan.accepts.has(principal.kind)          → throw toException(forbidden('PRINCIPAL_NOT_SUPPORTED'))   // P4 safety net (7.6)
 ├─ decision = await evaluator.evaluate(plan, principal, call, kernel)     // plan.requirements per invocation (7.2); a policy's 401 re-resolves with plan.accepts (8.1)
 │     deny → throw transport.toException(failureOf(decision), ctx)
 └─ return true
 (BetterAuthInfrastructureError / request-time BetterAuthConfigurationError:
    throw transport.toInternalException?.(error, ctx) ?? error        → 5xx on every transport, generic on GraphQL (§13.3))
```

The guard **never returns `false`**. A `false` return makes Nest throw an HTTP `ForbiddenException` on every transport, which Mercurius, WS and RPC then mis-deliver (R:nest-di §3.4, §5). The guard always throws the transport-native error.

**Order.** The plan comes first, because it needs only the class and the handler. v2 selected the transport first, so a `@Public()` handler in a context no transport serves (a credential-less TCP message, a third-party context type that global guards reach) answered 500 `NO_TRANSPORT` (REV2-NEST:`exp3-external-context-global-guard.mjs`). The origin check comes before resolution, as better-auth's router runs `validateOrigin` before the endpoint reads a session: a cross-site request costs no storage read, and no principal is memoized for a request that is denied anyway. v2's runtime comparison of the principal's kind with the handler's param decorators is gone: every plan comes from the planner, which checks it at boot (B15), including the kinds `defaultRequirements` name, now that the `planFor` subclass seam that produced unchecked plans is removed (§7.6).

Every comparison in this flow is between values extensions supplied: `principal.kind` against `plan.accepts` (source `kinds`, `@AcceptPrincipals`, `requires.principals`). Core names no kind and no credential scheme `[R1:NEST-r1-07]`.

### 7.2 Resolver contract and memoization (S7) `[A][B][C]` `[R1:NEST-r1-01, SEC-r1-13]` `[R2:NEST-r2-16, SEC-r2-07]`

The port is in §2.2.2. The default `ChainPrincipalResolver` keeps three memo scopes apart:

| Scope                                                                 | Keyed by                                                                                                                                                      | Holds                                                                                  | Lifetime                                                  |
| --------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------- |
| **Principal**                                                         | `(call.key, instance, freshness, plan.sourceSet)`; `(call.connection, …)` instead when `principalTtlMs > 0` and the plan's freshness is not `'authoritative'` | the resolution promise                                                                 | the logical request; a connection entry until `expiresAt` |
| **Policy I/O** (`AuthorizationContext.memo`, `PrincipalRequest.memo`) | `(call.key, instance, key)` where the key names concrete inputs as a serialized tuple (e.g. `["org:hasPermission","<orgId>",<permissions>]`)                  | promises of better-auth calls                                                          | the logical request, **never** a connection               |
| **Decision and per-invocation values**                                | `(call.invocation, instance, requirement expression)`                                                                                                         | the requirement's decision; values policies `provide()` (the resolved organization id) | one handler invocation                                    |

- **Storage.** `WeakMap<object, RequestState>` inside the singleton `RequestScope`. There is no module-level state and no DI request scope.
- **The principal promise is stored before it settles** `[A][B]`. GraphQL runs the guard once per root field, three times for three root fields in one request (R:nest-di §3.4; EXP-B:E8: 3 guard calls → **1** resolution). Concurrent invocations share one `getSession`. A rejection is memoized for the same request key too, so every root field fails the same way and a failing database sees no retry storm.
- **Decisions are per invocation, never per request or connection.** A requirement object is created once, when the decorator is evaluated, so v1's "memoize by requirement identity per request" let two aliased root fields asking about different organizations share one allow, and let a WebSocket connection with a principal TTL reuse an allow across messages. v2 keys decisions by `call.invocation`: the GraphQL field's `info`, the WS message's `args`, the HTTP request, the RPC context. Two guard runs of the **same** invocation (global guard plus `@UseBetterAuth()`) still share one decision. Policies that want cheap repeats dedupe their better-auth calls through `memo` keyed by their concrete inputs, so two identical checks cost one call and two different organizations cost two (Z6).
- **Source set.** The chain is filtered by the route's accepted kinds (§7.6). The planner records the filtered chain by **content**: the ordered indexes of the consulted sources in the instance's list, interned per instance (`RoutePlan.sourceSet`, e.g. `'0,2'`). That key is part of the principal key, so three root fields in three resolver methods with equal accepted kinds share one resolution, and root fields with different accepted kinds resolve each distinct set at most once. v2 said "the filtered list's identity", which a per-plan list would have split into one resolution per plan `[R2:NEST-r2-16]`.
- **Chain.** Resolution runs inside `handle.run({ cookies: call.cookies, forward: 'same-credential', inbound: call.headers, internal: true }, …)`, the same scope shape the evaluator uses (§8.1). That makes every nested better-auth call of every source cookie-aware (P2): refresh is suppressed where the transport cannot deliver cookies (§7.4), a `Set-Cookie` produced by a call that carries the request's own credential or none reaches the client through the bridge where it can, and the call is marked internal for hooks (§10.4). The built-in session source is the one exception, and it makes it itself: it wraps its `getSession` in a nested `run({ forward: 'none' })` and forwards that call's cookies through `returnHeaders`, so they are delivered exactly once (§7.3, ADR-09). A third-party source that also forwards a call's cookies by hand does the same; if it forgets, the kernel's cookie sink de-duplicates identical `Set-Cookie` values. The sources run in order: skip those whose `appliesTo` is false, stop at the first `authenticated` or `rejected`, and return `absent` if none applies (§4.3.3).
- **Connection entries** (WS, operations over a GraphQL WebSocket with `principalTtlMs > 0`). They store only settled `authenticated` and `absent` results, with an `expiresAt`. A `rejected` result (for example a transient 429) and an infrastructure failure are memoized per message only, and an infrastructure failure evicts the connection entry. A database blip therefore costs one failed message, not the TTL `[R1:SEC-r1-13]`. **Plans whose freshness is `'authoritative'` never use connection entries**: they resolve per message or per operation, so a TTL cannot delay a ban or a demotion on `@RequirePermission` handlers (§8.4) `[R2:SEC-r2-07]`.
- **`peek(call, request)`** returns the settled result without I/O. The scope interceptor and `BetterAuthService.principalFor(ctx)` use it.
- **`bypassMemo`** resolves once more, reading and writing no memo entry. Only the evaluator's re-classification of a 401 uses it (§8.1) `[R2:BA-r2-03]`.

| Transport                                                                                                                                           | `call.key` (principal, I/O memo)                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    | `call.invocation` (decisions, the invocation's own result)                           | `call.connection` (TTL reuse)                                                                                                                                       | Carrier (operation-wide results, §7.8)                                                 |
| --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| HTTP (Express, Fastify, third-party)                                                                                                                | the platform's `requests.key(req)` (Express `req`; Fastify `request.raw`)                                                                                                                                                                                                                                           | same                                                                                 | —                                                                                                                                                                   | the Nest request object (`args[0]`)                                                    |
| GraphQL query/mutation over HTTP                                                                                                                    | the underlying HTTP request key, **shared with the HTTP transport**                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                 | the field's `info` (`args[3]`), distinct per root field, alias and batched operation | —                                                                                                                                                                   | the GraphQL context (`args[2]`)                                                        |
| GraphQL operation over a WebSocket (every subscription; queries and mutations sent over graphql-ws or Mercurius `fullWsTransport`) `[R2:SEC-r2-03]` | the operation's context object (Apollo: graphql-ws calls a function-valued `context` once per subscribe message, graphql-ws 6.0.7 `dist/server-3ewaJSjp.js:206-207` and 6.2.1 `dist/server-DHPI7HHW.js:207-208`, the versions @nestjs/graphql 13.2.4 and 14.0.0 pin; Mercurius: a new copy per operation, LEAD-V35) | `info`                                                                               | the connection's upgrade request (Apollo `extra.request`; Mercurius the object `mercuriusSubscriptionContext()` stores), only with `subscriptionPrincipalTtlMs > 0` | the GraphQL context                                                                    |
| WebSocket (socket.io, ws)                                                                                                                           | the per-message `args` array (shared by all guards of a message, LEAD-V7)                                                                                                                                                                                                                                           | same                                                                                 | the socket                                                                                                                                                          | **none**: decorators read the scope (the socket would race across concurrent messages) |
| RPC                                                                                                                                                 | `switchToRpc().getContext()` (one object per message; gRPC: the per-call `Metadata`)                                                                                                                                                                                                                                | same                                                                                 | —                                                                                                                                                                   | the same object                                                                        |

### 7.3 Built-in session source (S2) `[A][B][C]` `[R2:BA-r2-01, BA-r2-06]`

```ts
export const SESSION_PRINCIPAL_KIND = "session" as const;

export const sessionPrincipal = <S = AuthSession>(
  options: SessionPrincipalOptions<S> = {},
) =>
  definePrincipalSource<SessionPrincipal>({
    id: "better-auth:session",
    kinds: [SESSION_PRINCIPAL_KIND],
    acceptance: "default", // every authenticated route
    credentialHeaders: ["cookie", "authorization"], // bridge comparison and redaction (7.5, 13.4)
    async resolve(r) {
      const ctx = await r.auth.context();
      const stateful = Boolean(
        ctx.options.database || ctx.options.secondaryStorage,
      ); // mirrors hasServerSessionStore
      const authoritative = r.freshness === "authoritative";
      const query: { disableCookieCache?: true; disableRefresh?: true } = {};
      if (authoritative && stateful) query.disableCookieCache = true; // stateless: the cookie IS the session
      if (r.cookies === null) query.disableRefresh = true; // belt; the plugin's skip flag is the braces (7.4)

      let result: { headers?: Headers | null; response: unknown };
      try {
        // forward: 'none' → this call's cookies are forwarded exactly once, through returnHeaders (no bridge duplicate)
        result = await r.auth.run(
          { cookies: r.cookies, forward: "none", internal: true },
          () =>
            r.auth.api.getSession({
              headers: r.headers,
              returnHeaders: true,
              query,
            }),
        );
      } catch (e) {
        const failure = AuthFailures.fromAPIError(e); // 401/403/429 (bad x-api-key, failed refresh, api-key rate limit + Retry-After)
        if (!failure) throw e; // ≥500 or non-APIError → infrastructure (S6)
        const cleanup = apiErrorSetCookies(e); // e.headers + hidden better-call:api-error-headers
        if (r.cookies && cleanup.length) r.cookies.append(cleanup);
        return rejected(failure);
      }
      if (r.cookies) {
        const setCookie = result.headers?.getSetCookie() ?? []; // a before-hook short-circuit returns no Headers (LEAD-V37)
        if (setCookie.length) r.cookies.append(setCookie); // ONLY set-cookie: never cache-control / pragma
      }
      if (result.response == null) return absent();
      // Authoritative: only what the get-session endpoint itself produced, never a session a before-hook supplied (an API key's
      // mocked session, a short-circuiting hook). That is the set better-auth's getAuthoritativeSessionFromCtx accepts (LEAD-V36, LEAD-EXP-8).
      if (authoritative && !r.auth.producedByEndpoint(result.response))
        return absent();
      const userId = (options.userId ?? defaultUserId)(result.response as S); // default s.user?.id; customSession → session.userId option
      if (userId === null)
        throw BetterAuthConfigurationError.atRequest(
          "SESSION_USER_ID",
          "session.userId returned null for a resolved session",
        );
      return authenticated({
        kind: SESSION_PRINCIPAL_KIND,
        source: "better-auth:session",
        userId,
        session: result.response as S,
      });
    },
    // jwt without disableSettingJwtHeader, bearer without requireSignature, and (api-key plugin present) W_API_KEY_FULL_SESSION /
    // W_API_KEY_SESSION_MULTIPLIER, which also reads ctx.policies and options.apiKeySessions (7.9, 8.3.1)
    advise: (ctx) => costHints(ctx, options),
  });
```

- **`returnHeaders: true`** keeps the refresh and cookie-cache `Set-Cookie`s that a plain call drops. There are 9 code paths (R:ba-core §4.3). EXP-C1's baseline with `updateAge: 0` emits `session_token`. It works for `customSession` too, because it is a dispatch-level feature (`BA/api/dispatch.ts:467-477`).
- **A short-circuited dispatch returns no `Headers`.** When a before-hook answers `/get-session` itself (the api-key plugin with `enableSessionForAPIKeys`, or a Nest `@BeforeAuth('/get-session')` hook returning an object, §10.5), better-auth returns `{ headers: undefined, response }` unless a hook set a response header (LEAD-V37). v2 dereferenced the headers and answered 500 for every such request on cookie-capable transports (REV2-BA:`exp1-apikey-returnheaders.mjs`). `AuthLike.api.getSession` types the result accordingly (§11.3), and `S-short-circuit-session` pins it `[R2:BA-r2-01]`.
- **Only `set-cookie` is forwarded.** `getSession` also returns `cache-control: no-store` and `pragma: no-cache`, which must not leak onto app responses (R:ba-core §4.3). EXP-A:`exp-e2e.mjs` verified one `session_token` and `cache-control=null` on a guarded route on all four platform × major combinations.
- **Credential translation happens inside `getSession`.** Bearer, api-key session mocks (`enableSessionForAPIKeys`), jwt side effects, multi-session and `customSession` all take effect through better-auth's own hooks, so the source never parses credentials (R1). Hooks see the original request: the bearer plugin's cookie rewrite happens inside the dispatch and is invisible to other before-hooks (LEAD-V23).
- **`authoritative` accepts what better-auth's authoritative read accepts** `[R2:BA-r2-06]`. better-auth's admin and sensitive endpoints read the session with `getAuthoritativeSessionFromCtx`, which discards a session a hook placed in the context and re-reads through the plain `getSession()` function, where no hook runs (LEAD-V36). A key-mocked session therefore never reaches them: every admin endpoint answers 401 for a key under `enableSessionForAPIKeys` (REV2-BA:`exp6-apikey-session-admin.mjs`). v2's authoritative read went through the hook pipeline and accepted the mock, so a narrow CI key passed `@RequirePermission` with its owner's admin role. The source now keeps the two parts of better-auth's rule: the cookie cache is bypassed when a server-side store exists (`BA/api/routes/session.ts:520-539`) `[C]`, and the session must be one the get-session endpoint produced. The `nestjs()` plugin observes that: its after-hook records the object an endpoint returned, and a before-hook short-circuit skips every after-hook (LEAD-V37, §10.2). LEAD-EXP-8 compared the record with better-auth's own verdict for cookie, bearer, key-session, short-circuit and replaced-result requests, with and without `customSession`, on 1.7.0 and 1.7.4: they agree in every case but one. A request carrying both a session cookie and an API key is answered as the key's owner by better-auth's ordinary endpoints and as the cookie's user by its admin endpoints; the kernel answers `absent` (401) on an authoritative route, the stricter of the two (RK27). Routes with the default freshness accept a key session, exactly as better-auth's `sessionMiddleware` endpoints do (§8.3.1).
- **The user-id mapping lives in the source** (`session.userId` runtime option), not in `AuthHandle`, so core has no notion of a session shape `[R1:NEST-r1-07]`.

### 7.4 Cookie forwarding and refresh suppression per transport capability (S2)

`getSession` emits `Set-Cookie` on 9 code paths (R:ba-core §4.3). Two of them move server or cookie state:

- **row 7, sliding refresh:** the DB `expiresAt` is extended and `session_token` is re-set;
- **row 4, stateless refresh-cache:** `session_data` is re-issued and `session_token` is re-set, with no DB write.

If the cookie cannot be delivered, the browser cookie expires before the server session, which is the drift better-auth works to avoid (`BA/api/state/should-session-refresh.ts:3-10`; `nextCookies`). Where the transport can deliver cookies, they are forwarded. Where it cannot, the refresh itself is suppressed, not just its cookies dropped.

| Caller                                                                                                                   | `call.cookies`                                                                                                               | Session source / call                       | Refresh                                                    | Forwarded to client                                                                                                                                             |
| ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| HTTP controller (Express, Fastify, third-party)                                                                          | platform sink                                                                                                                | `returnHeaders: true`                       | normal                                                     | `set-cookie` only                                                                                                                                               |
| GraphQL query/mutation over HTTP (Apollo, Mercurius)                                                                     | the HTTP sink: Express `req.res`; Fastify `requests.responseFor(req)` (root `onRequest` map, LEAD-V8); Mercurius `ctx.reply` | same                                        | normal                                                     | `set-cookie` only                                                                                                                                               |
| GraphQL operation over a WebSocket (subscriptions; queries and mutations over graphql-ws or Mercurius `fullWsTransport`) | `null`                                                                                                                       | + `disableRefresh`, + skip flag             | **suppressed**                                             | none                                                                                                                                                            |
| WebSocket (socket.io, ws)                                                                                                | `null`                                                                                                                       | same                                        | **suppressed**                                             | none                                                                                                                                                            |
| RPC (all carriers)                                                                                                       | `null`                                                                                                                       | same                                        | **suppressed**                                             | none                                                                                                                                                            |
| Library policies (org, admin) and third-party principal sources in a request                                             | the transport's sink or `null`                                                                                               | `auth.api.*` with the request's own headers | normal / **suppressed**                                    | `set-cookie` via the plugin bridge (same credential or none)                                                                                                    |
| Direct `auth.api.*` in a handler or service (under the scope interceptor, §7.5)                                          | the transport's sink or `null`                                                                                               | the user's call                             | better-auth default / **suppressed** in cookie-less scopes | **none by default**; with `@ForwardAuthCookies()` / `forwardDirectCalls` / `forwardCookies(fn)`: `set-cookie` of calls carrying the caller's credential or none |
| Direct call outside any scope (cron, queue worker, bootstrap seeding)                                                    | none                                                                                                                         | the user's call                             | better-auth default                                        | none. Use `returnHeaders`, or `service.withoutCookies(fn)` to suppress                                                                                          |

**How suppression works** `[A][B][C]`. It is construction-time plugin behavior, following the `nextCookies` precedent. The `nestjs()` plugin registers one before-hook:

- **matcher:** `ctx._flag !== 'router' && binding?.current()?.cookies === null`;
- **handler:** `await setShouldSkipSessionRefresh(true)`.

This is the only public way to set that flag. It lives in better-auth request state, which exists only inside a better-auth dispatch. `better-auth/api` exports the setter (LEAD-V2) but not `runWithRequestState`, which lives in `@better-auth/core/context`. A before-hook runs inside the dispatch's own store, so the flag lands exactly where `getSession` reads it (EXP-C1: "plugin skip-refresh set-cookie: []").

**Stateless refresh-cache branch.** Without a database or secondary storage, better-auth force-enables `cookieCache` with `refreshCache` (`BA/context/create-context.ts:104-116`). That branch checks **only** `getShouldSkipSessionRefresh()` (`BA/api/routes/session.ts:199-204`, LEAD-V3). `query.disableRefresh` returns early only later (`:309`), so on its own it does **not** stop the branch. EXP-A:`exp-plugin.mjs` and EXP-B:E2 show this:

- control, `disableRefresh` only: `session_data` and `session_token` emitted;
- with the skip flag: none emitted.

The session source still passes `disableRefresh: true` on cookie-less calls as a belt, because it also skips rows 6 and 9 (a pointless cookie-cache write).

**Why any path, not just `/get-session`.** `nextCookies` suppresses only on `/get-session` (LEAD-V14), but plugin endpoints that read the session internally slide it too. Policies call `hasPermission` and `getActiveMember`, for example. EXP-B:E3, re-run by A and C:

- without a scope, `getActiveMember` emits `session_token` and moves the DB expiry;
- inside a cookie-less scope, neither happens.

The matcher therefore covers every non-router call made inside a cookie-less scope.

**Cleanup cookies** (rows 1, 2, 3 and 5: expire a stale cache or delete an invalid token) are still computed by better-auth. On cookie-less transports they are dropped harmlessly, and the next cookie-capable request cleans up again.

**The plugin is mandatory** (B03). Without it the stateless branch and nested plugin-endpoint refreshes could not be suppressed, and the library's own policy calls could not forward the refreshed cookies they produce. That would be two behavior modes users cannot see (ADR-02).

### 7.5 Direct `auth.api.*` calls in application code `[A][C]` `[R1:BA-r1-02, SEC-r1-03]`

`BetterAuthScopeInterceptor`, a global `APP_INTERCEPTOR` registered with `useExisting`, handles each handler invocation:

1. It selects the transport and builds `call` (sync).
2. It opens `RequestScope.run({ cookies: call.cookies, forward: plan.forwardDirectCalls ? 'same-credential' : 'none', inbound: call.headers, internal: false, plan, resolutions }, …)` around the _subscription_ to `next.handle()`. `resolutions` holds the result the guard produced for this invocation (a `peek()` under the plan's memo key, or the invocation's stamp, §7.8); a public plan carries none:

```ts
intercept(ctx: ExecutionContext, next: CallHandler) {
  const scope = this.scopes.forExecution(ctx);                     // null when no transport handles ctx
  return scope ? new Observable((sub) => scope.run(() => next.handle().subscribe(sub))) : next.handle();
}
```

Nest invokes the handler and its param factories inside the interceptor chain (`router-execution-context.js:40-46`; WS: LEAD-V7), and `InterceptorsConsumer` binds each step with `AsyncResource`.

**Default: better-auth's server-call semantics.** A direct `auth.api.*` call from a handler or a service behaves as it does in plain better-auth: its `Set-Cookie` is **not** written to the caller's response. The one change is in cookie-less scopes (WS, RPC, subscriptions), where refresh is suppressed because nothing could deliver the cookie (S2). In plain better-auth a server call never touches the browser unless the developer adds a cookie plugin (`nextCookies`) or uses `returnHeaders`/`asResponse`. v1 forwarded every direct call, so an admin handler that ran `auth.api.signUpEmail({ body })` (auto sign-in is on by default) swapped the admin's browser session for the new user's (BA-r1-02), and a service that called `getSession` with a service-account bearer token could hand that session to the end user (REV-SEC:`probe-bridge-foreign.mjs`) `[R1]`.

**Opt-in forwarding** for handlers that proxy the caller's own login or logout:

- per handler or controller: `@ForwardAuthCookies()` (and `@ForwardAuthCookies(false)` to opt one handler out of a controller-level opt-in);
- per instance: `cookies: { forwardDirectCalls: true }` (B28 warns, because it applies to every handler);
- per call site: `service.forwardCookies(() => this.auth.api.signInEmail({ body, headers }))`.

**Credential matching** (plugin entry 5, §10.2). Where forwarding is on, the bridge forwards a direct call's `Set-Cookie` only if the call carried **no credential** (a login or sign-up) or **the caller's own credential**. The credential is compared as a triple: the session-token cookie, found by name through `$context.authCookies.sessionToken.name` and parsed with better-auth's `parseCookies`; the `authorization` header; and the values of every source's `credentialHeaders` (for example `x-api-key`). Anything else is dropped and logged once at debug with the endpoint path. Deliberate account switching (impersonation, "sign in as") uses `service.forwardCookies(fn, { anyCredential: true })`.

**Library-internal calls always forward.** The resolver chain (§7.2) and the evaluator (§8.1) both run in `forward: 'same-credential'` scopes. Policies and principal sources call `auth.api.*` with the request's own headers, so their cookies (for example a sliding refresh inside `hasPermission`) are the caller's own and reach the browser on cookie-capable transports: the credential matches. One exception is harmless: for a bearer client, the bearer plugin's before-hook adds the session cookie to the call's headers inside the dispatch (`BA/plugins/bearer/index.ts:100-115`), so the bridge sees a credential triple that differs from the inbound one and drops that call's `Set-Cookie`, which a bearer client does not use anyway (`reviews/round-2-BA.md`, BA's observation on BA-r1-02; the credential-matching unit test expects the drop, §14.5). A third-party source that presents a credential other than the request's gets that call's cookies dropped, like any foreign credential. The session source's own `getSession` is the one internal call that runs with the bridge off, because it forwards through `returnHeaders` (§7.3).

**Direct credential endpoints bypass better-auth's router protections.** A server-side `auth.api.signInEmail({ body })` skips better-auth's rate limiter and origin check, which run only in the router (`BA/api/index.ts:285-292, 310`; LEAD-V16). The docs therefore recommend letting clients call better-auth's own routes (through the mount) for sign-in, sign-up and password flows, and keeping direct credential calls for trusted back-office code. A handler that does proxy them should apply the app's own throttling. `@ForwardAuthCookies()` is required for its cookies to reach the browser at all, so the pattern is always an explicit choice.

- **Why an interceptor rather than a platform-level scope opened at `init$`** (drafts B, C; ADR-11):
  - it is transport-neutral;
  - it runs after body parsing;
  - it gives param decorators a race-free source on WebSockets, where the per-message `args` array is not visible to param factories (LEAD-V7);
  - it keeps the platform contract small.

  An early scope would survive Express parsing (LEAD-V11), but it would cover HTTP only.

- **Coverage gaps, documented.** Code in middleware, in guards (including other libraries' guards) and in policies runs outside the scope. So do GraphQL field resolvers unless `fieldResolverEnhancers` includes `'interceptors'` (their continuations run outside the root resolver's scope), and gateways without `@UseBetterAuth()` (which B16 rejects). Such code gets plain better-auth semantics for direct calls; it can use `service.withoutCookies(fn)` or its own `returnHeaders`. Decorators there fall back to the stamps (§7.8). `BetterAuthService.getPrincipal()` throws `NO_AUTH_SCOPE` there; a guard or interceptor reads the principal with `service.principalFor(ctx)` (§7.8) `[R2:NEST-r2-07]`.
- **Opting out entirely.** `service.runOutsideScope(fn)` runs `fn` as if no scope existed: no forwarding and no suppression `[C]`.
- **Committed responses.** If a handler has already sent the response itself (`@Res()` plus a manual send), the sink reports `false`. The bridge then logs one debug line and drops the cookies.

### 7.6 Public, optional and required semantics; accepted principal kinds `[A][B][C]`

**Plan compilation** (`RoutePlanner`, cached per (controller class, handler)) `[R2:NEST-r2-01, NEST-r2-04, NEST-r2-08]`:

0. **Cache key.** Plans are cached in a `WeakMap<Type, WeakMap<Function, RoutePlan>>` keyed by `ctx.getClass()`, then `ctx.getHandler()`, and never by the handler alone. Nest hands every subclass the **same** handler function for an inherited route method (REV2-NEST:`exp1-inherited-handler.mjs`, 11.1.17 and 12.0.1), while the plan depends on the class chain. v2 cached per handler, so in `abstract class CrudController { @Get() list() {} }` with a `@Public()` subclass and a `@RequirePermission` subclass, whichever route was requested first decided the other's plan. The boot scan compiles the same (class, method) pairs.
1. Read the access decorator (`@Public` / `@OptionalAuth` / `@RequireAuth`), `@AcceptPrincipals`, `@SkipOriginCheck`, `@ForwardAuthCookies` and the requirements at the **method** level and at the **class** level. For the class level, use the own metadata of each class in the prototype chain, most-derived first.
2. **Same-level contradiction** fails boot (B15). `@Public()` or `@OptionalAuth()` together with requirements at the same level is contradictory: an anonymous caller can never satisfy a principal requirement.
3. **Effective access** is decided by the closest level that says anything:
   - the method's access decorator; else
   - `'required'` if the method has requirements; else
   - the class's access decorator; else
   - `'required'` if the class has requirements; else
   - the first registered transport whose `defaultAccessFor(class, method)` answers: `'inherit'` for GraphQL field resolvers (§9.2) `[R2:NEST-r2-04]`; else
   - `defaultAccess`.
4. **Effective requirements.** If access is `'required'`, they are the instance's `defaultRequirements`, then class requirements (base first), then method requirements, in declaration order. Otherwise there are none. A method-level `@Public()` or `@OptionalAuth()` is therefore an explicit, visible opt-out of class-level requirements (§17 Q3), and of `defaultRequirements` too. `defaultRequirements` replaces v2's protected `BetterAuthGuard.planFor` seam: an overriding subclass could not be registered at the global guard, at `@UseBetterAuth()` sites or in the coverage check, its plans escaped boot validation, and the scope interceptor and decorators read different plans than the guard. A runtime option compiled into every plan has none of these gaps `[R2:NEST-r2-08]`.
5. **Accepted kinds** `[R1:SEC-r1-02, BA-r1-01]`:
   - the kinds named by the closest `@AcceptPrincipals(...)` (method over class); otherwise the instance's _default kinds_, the `kinds` of every source with `acceptance: 'default'` (by default only `'session'`);
   - **plus** every kind that an effective requirement names, through `requirement.principals ?? policy.requires.principals`. `@RequireApiKeyPermission(p)` therefore admits `'api-key'` on its route without a second decorator, and only policies that can judge a kind make it reachable.

   A source whose kinds are all outside the set is not consulted for the route (§4.3.3). An API key or OAuth token therefore authenticates nothing on a route that did not ask for it: no quota is spent and the request is treated as if the header were absent. The consulted sources are recorded by content as `sourceSet` (§7.2).

6. **Principal param constraints.** Each `definePrincipalParam` decorator on the handler contributes `{ kind, reason }`. A handler that accepts kinds its param decorator rejects fails boot (B15 `PRINCIPAL_PARAM_CONFLICT`, hint: `@CurrentPrincipal()`). Every plan comes from the planner, lazily compiled ones included (§5.4), so no principal of a rejected kind reaches such a decorator, and the guard carries no runtime comparison for it.
7. **Freshness** is `'authoritative'` if `@RequireAuth({ authoritative: true })` is present at the effective level, `session.freshness` says so, or any effective requirement has `freshIdentity` (from the requirement or its policy; the admin policy, §8.4) `[R1:SEC-r1-04]`. An `'inherit'` plan has the instance's default freshness.
8. **Origin check** is `'off'` with `@SkipOriginCheck()` (method or class) or `originCheck.mode: 'off'`; otherwise `'form'` when direct-call forwarding is on for the handler, else `'cookie'` (§7.10) `[R2:SEC-r2-08]`. **Direct-call forwarding** follows `@ForwardAuthCookies` (method over class), else `cookies.forwardDirectCalls`.

| Effective access                        | Principal I/O                                         | No credentials        | Presented but invalid credential (e.g. bad `x-api-key` on a route accepting keys) | Infrastructure failure | `@CurrentSession()`                     |
| --------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------- | --------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------- | --------------------------------------- |
| `required` (default)                    | yes                                                   | 401 `UNAUTHENTICATED` | denial with better-auth's status and `reason`                                     | 5xx                    | `AuthSession`                           |
| `optional` (`@OptionalAuth()`)          | yes                                                   | allowed               | **denial** (a bad credential is never downgraded to anonymous)                    | 5xx                    | `AuthSession \| null`                   |
| `public` (`@Public()`)                  | **none**                                              | allowed               | not inspected                                                                     | cannot happen (no I/O) | boot error B15                          |
| `inherit` (a transport's default, §9.2) | **none**: the enclosing operation's guard run decided | allowed               | not inspected                                                                     | cannot happen (no I/O) | the enclosing operation's result (§7.8) |

`@Public()` doing zero I/O fixes reference issue #159: health probes no longer return 500 when the database is down. It also means a bad API key on a public route consumes no quota (R:ba-authz §4.2 #5). `@OptionalAuth()` is the "attach the session if present" mode.

**Public means no identity** `[R2:SEC-r2-04]`. `BetterAuthService.getPrincipal()` and `getSession()` return `null` in a public handler: they never start a resolution anywhere (§7.8). In v2 they resolved lazily there, so a cross-site form post to a `@Public()` unsafe route that called `getSession()` acted as the victim without any origin check, because the guard returns before the check on public plans. A handler that wants the caller's identity when there is one uses `@OptionalAuth()`, which resolves in the guard, after the origin check (§17 Q27). The one public case that needs the origin check without an identity, a login proxy, gets it through `@ForwardAuthCookies()` (§7.10).

```ts
@Controller("reports")
export class ReportsController {
  @Get() list(@CurrentSession() s: AuthSession) {} // sessions only (default kinds)

  @AcceptPrincipals("session", "api-key") // both; read the union
  @Get("export")
  export(@CurrentPrincipal() p: AuthPrincipal) {}

  @RequireApiKeyPermission({ reports: ["read"] }) // admits 'api-key' by itself
  @Get("feed")
  feed() {}
}
```

### 7.7 Error semantics (S6)

| Situation                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                               | Result                                                                                                                                                                 |
| --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| No principal on a required route                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        | 401 `UNAUTHENTICATED`                                                                                                                                                  |
| A source returns `rejected` (for example `APIError` 401/403 from `getSession` hooks, or an API-key result mapped per §8.3.1)                                                                                                                                                            | that status; `code` `UNAUTHENTICATED` (401) or `FORBIDDEN` (403); `reason` = better-auth code; cleanup cookies forwarded where possible; the chain stops               |
| Rate limited during resolution: an `APIError` 429 from `getSession` hooks (api-key with `enableSessionForAPIKeys`), or `verifyApiKey` reporting `RATE_LIMITED`/`USAGE_EXCEEDED`                                                                                                         | 429 `RATE_LIMITED`; `Retry-After` from the error's headers or from `details.tryAgainIn` (ms, rounded up to seconds) when present `[R1:BA-r1-04, SEC-r1-05]`            |
| A principal of a kind the route does not accept (a source that broke P4)                                                                                                                                                                                                                | 403 `PRINCIPAL_NOT_SUPPORTED`                                                                                                                                          |
| A policy's better-auth call answers 401 for an authenticated principal (better-auth's session middleware lost the session, or storage failed and it swallowed the error, LEAD-V36)                                                                                                      | re-classified once (§8.1): the principal still resolves authoritatively → 5xx; it does not → 401 `UNAUTHENTICATED` with better-auth's code as `reason` `[R2:BA-r2-03]` |
| Unsafe operation whose browser leg carries a cookie, from an untrusted or missing origin; a login proxy's cross-site navigation                                                                                                                                                         | 403 `FORBIDDEN`, `reason` `INVALID_ORIGIN` / `MISSING_OR_NULL_ORIGIN` / `CROSS_SITE_NAVIGATION_LOGIN_BLOCKED` (better-auth's codes, §7.10)                             |
| `APIError` ≥ 500, `BetterAuthError`, DB or network errors, anything else                                                                                                                                                                                                                | `BetterAuthInfrastructureError` → 5xx, logged once with a redacted cause (§13.4); **never 401/403**                                                                    |
| Configuration faults met at request time (unknown transport; `customSession` without `userId` at runtime; a lazily loaded handler with an invalid plan; a param decorator or `getPrincipal()` on a handler the guard did not run for; `getPrincipal()` outside any handler scope, §7.8) | `BetterAuthConfigurationError.atRequest` → 500; the message is generic as thrown, so it stays generic on GraphQL even where no transport maps it (§13.3)               |
| Public route during a DB outage                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                         | unaffected (never resolves)                                                                                                                                            |

Detection is always `isAPIError` from `better-auth/api`, which accepts both `APIError` classes and `name === "APIError"` (LEAD-V5). It is never `instanceof`, because better-call's CJS and ESM copies have different classes (R:ba-core §4.2).

**Known upstream limitations.**

- RK2: better-auth turns storage errors into "no session" in two places: `customSession` catches errors from its inner `getSession` (`BA/plugins/custom-session/index.ts:100-107`), and `getSessionFromCtx`, which every `sessionMiddleware` endpoint uses, catches every error (LEAD-V36). For the guard's own read in a `customSession` app a storage outage therefore looks like 401 instead of a 5xx; we cannot fix that without reimplementing `getSession`, which R1 forbids. For policy calls into session-middleware endpoints the kernel does not pass the 401 on as a denial (§8.1) `[R2:BA-r2-03]`. Both are documented, and the upstream proposal asks better-auth to rethrow non-`APIError` failures there.
- RK18: `verifyApiKey` reports a storage outage as `INVALID_API_KEY` (LEAD-V20). `apiKeyPrincipal()` mitigates this with an outage probe (§8.3.1) and we will propose an upstream change.

### 7.8 Accessing the principal `[R2:NEST-r2-06, NEST-r2-07, NEST-r2-14, SEC-r2-04]`

**Param decorators are synchronous** (async factories only work without pipes, R:nest-di §4.3). `@CurrentSession()`, `@CurrentUser()`, `@CurrentPrincipal()` and any decorator built with `definePrincipalParam` look up the resolution for the handler plan's instance (`@UseAuthInstance`, read from metadata; the decorators take no `instance` option, NEST-r2-14) in this order:

1. **The scope** opened by `BetterAuthScopeInterceptor`, which holds the result the guard produced for this invocation (a `peek()` under the plan's memo key) and the invocation's published values. It is race-free on every transport `[L]`. Where `peek()` has no result for the instance, the interceptor fills the scope from the invocation stamp, a single carrier entry (item 2) or a test stamp (item 3), so a replaced guard works on WebSockets too.
2. **The stamps** `[A]`, written by the real guard, for readers without the interceptor (HTTP, GraphQL and RPC handlers where the interceptor is not applied; GraphQL field resolvers, which run outside the root field's scope):
   - the **invocation stamp**: `Symbol.for(…:resolution)` on `call.invocation` holds the result of **this** invocation's guard run, one per instance, next to the per-invocation values under `Symbol.for(…:invocation)` (e.g. GraphQL `info`). A reader whose own guard ran takes it and nothing else;
   - the **carrier stamp**: `Symbol.for(…:resolution)` on the operation-wide carrier (the GraphQL context) holds a `Map<instance, Map<memoKey, PrincipalResult>>`, one entry per distinct (freshness, source set) that root fields of the operation resolved. A reader without its own guard run (a field resolver with an `inherit` plan) takes an entry only when the instance has **exactly one**; with several (root fields with different `@AcceptPrincipals` or freshness in one operation) it throws `NO_AUTH_RESULT` with the hint to give the field resolver its own access or to read the principal in the root field. v2 kept one entry per instance on the carrier, last writer wins, so a field resolver under a session-only root field could read an API-key principal that a sibling root field admitted (NEST-r2-06).

   WS has no carrier on purpose: its invocation is the per-message `args` array, which the interceptor sees.

3. **The test stamp** `[R1:NEST-r1-08]`, written by `stampPrincipal()` and by the `overrideAuthGuard` stand-in guard (§14.8). Neither knows the transport, so the stamp is a record `{ elements, results }` under `Symbol.for('nestjs-slightly-better-auth:test-stamp')`, where `elements` is a copy of the stamping guard's `ctx.getArgs()` and `results` a `Map<instance, PrincipalResult>`. It is attached to that args array and to each of its extensible object elements. A reader (the scope interceptors and these decorators) looks on its own args array first, then on each object element, and accepts a record only if `elements` is element-wise identical (`===`) to its own `ctx.getArgs()`:
   - on GraphQL, RPC and WebSockets the guards and interceptors of one invocation share the args array itself (LEAD-V7, LEAD-V34), so the interceptor finds the record there and copies it into the scope it opens. This is the WebSocket path: gateways always have the interceptor (B16), and the socket-level copy is never needed;
   - on HTTP the router hands guards and interceptors separate `[req, res, next]` arrays with the same elements (LEAD-V34), so the record is found on `req` and still matches;
   - a record on a shared object (a socket, a GraphQL root value) does not match a sibling request, field or message, whose elements differ. The one theoretical collision, two concurrent messages with identical primitive payloads on one socket stamped with different principals, would matter only to a reader without the interceptor, which gateways never lack.

   Like every stamp, the record is symbol-keyed, so no parsed request payload can carry one.

4. **Otherwise** throw `BetterAuthConfigurationError.atRequest('NO_AUTH_RESULT', 'No authentication result: BetterAuthGuard did not run (globalGuard: false without @UseBetterAuth(), or a guard replaced in a test without stampPrincipal())', { site: 'SiteController.method' })`. This surfaces reference issue #12 as a clear error instead of an `undefined`. The decorator runs where the guard did not, so no transport's `toInternalException` can map this error, and a GraphQL driver copies `message` into the response. The error is therefore safe as thrown `[R1:SEC-r1-19]`: its `message` is the fixed `Authentication is misconfigured`, `extensions.reason` is `AUTH_MISCONFIGURED`, and the site, detail and hint are ordinary own properties, which Nest's exception layer logs (LEAD-V31) and neither GraphQL driver serializes (LEAD-EXP-7). A `defineInvocationParam` decorator with nothing published throws the same way, with its `missing` text as the `detail` (`NO_INVOCATION_VALUE`), and so does every other request-time configuration error, including one raised by `BetterAuthService.getPrincipal()` in a resolver body (§13.1). Since v3, B16 does fail boot for a claimed handler with such a decorator that no guard covers (§5.4) `[R2:NEST-r2-02]`, but that does not make the case unreachable. Coverage cannot be proven for every call site: a claim whose severity the user relaxed to `'warn'` or `'off'`, handlers in lazily loaded modules, guards applied through another library's composite guard, and guards replaced in tests all get past it. The error itself must therefore be safe as thrown, and `T-internal-error-generic` reaches it through a replaced guard.

**What each decorator returns:**

- `@CurrentSession()` `[R1:NEST-r1-10]` returns `principal.session` for a principal of kind `'session'`, or `null` on an optional route with no principal. It is built with `definePrincipalParam({ kind: SESSION_PRINCIPAL_KIND, reason: 'SESSION_REQUIRED', project: (p) => p.session })` by the session unit. The planner records the kind as data, and a route that could admit another kind fails boot (B15), so the handler never receives a `null` typed as `AuthSession`. It is named `CurrentSession` rather than v1's `Session` because `@nestjs/common` exports a `Session` route-param decorator (it injects `req.session`), and an IDE auto-import into a file that already imports from `@nestjs/common` silently picked the wrong one.
- `@CurrentUser()` behaves the same way and returns `principal.session.user`.
- `@CurrentPrincipal()` returns `AuthPrincipal | null` and has no kind constraint.
- `@ActiveOrganizationId()` and `@ActiveMemberRole()` (`./organization`) are `defineInvocationParam` decorators. They return the value the org policy published for **this invocation** (§8.3), never a value from a sibling GraphQL field.

**Services** use `BetterAuthService.getPrincipal()` or `getSession()` inside a handler scope. They **never start a resolution** `[R2:SEC-r2-04]`: they return the result the guard produced for the invocation (the scope's entry), `null` on a public plan (§7.6), and throw `NO_AUTH_RESULT` when the guard did not run for the handler. Calling them in a guarded handler costs nothing. **Outside any handler scope** (a guard, middleware, a policy, a GraphQL field resolver without `'interceptors'` in `fieldResolverEnhancers`, a background job) they throw `BetterAuthConfigurationError.atRequest('NO_AUTH_SCOPE', …)`: v2 returned `null` there, the same value as "anonymous", so a migrated `SubscriptionActiveGuard` rejected every paying user and a throttler keyed by user id put everyone in one bucket (NEST-r2-07).

**Guards and interceptors** that run after `BetterAuthGuard` read the principal with `BetterAuthService.principalFor(context)` `[R2:NEST-r2-07]`. It is synchronous and never performs I/O: it compiles or fetches the plan for `(context.getClass(), context.getHandler())`, and when the plan belongs to the service's instance it returns the resolver's settled entry under the plan's memo key (`peek` through the transport's `describe`), else the invocation or carrier stamp by the rules above, else a test stamp; `undefined` means the guard has not resolved one (it runs later, the plan is public or inherited without a single carrier entry, or another instance owns the plan). The migration recipe for `request.user` in custom guards uses it (§15.2):

```ts
@Injectable()
export class SubscriptionActiveGuard implements CanActivate {
  constructor(
    @Inject(BETTER_AUTH_SERVICE) private readonly auth: BetterAuthService,
  ) {}
  canActivate(ctx: ExecutionContext) {
    const r = this.auth.principalFor(ctx); // BetterAuthGuard (global or @UseBetterAuth()) ran first
    return (
      r?.outcome === "authenticated" &&
      r.principal.kind === "session" &&
      r.principal.session.user.plan === "pro"
    );
  }
}
```

### 7.9 Cost per protected request

- **Session resolution.** One `getSession` per request, shared by all guard invocations, decorators and services. That is 0 storage reads on a cookie-cache hit, otherwise 1 read, plus 1 write when a refresh is due (R:ba-authz §1.0). An authoritative route (admin permission by default, §8.4) always reads storage once.
- **Public routes.** Zero.
- **API keys through `apiKeyPrincipal()`.** One `verifyApiKey` per request, on routes that accept keys only. Each verification counts against the key's usage and rate limit and writes to storage (usage counter, `updatedAt`) `[R1:SEC-r1-14]`. Org policies deny `'api-key'` principals without calling better-auth.
- **Rare paths.** The API-key outage probe (one read and one no-op write, at most once per second per instance, §8.3.1); the re-classification of a 401 a policy call met (one authoritative resolution, §8.1); the default organization ref for a `customSession` shape without `session.activeOrganizationId` (one `getActiveMember` per request, §8.3).
- **Multipliers,** surfaced as boot advice (B21) by the units that know about them:
  - the jwt plugin without `disableSettingJwtHeader: true` signs a JWT and reads `jwks` on every `getSession` (session unit);
  - bearer without `requireSignature: true` pays a lookup for foreign tokens (session unit);
  - `apiKey({ enableSessionForAPIKeys: true })` validates the key on **every** better-auth call that carries it, not only `getSession` (LEAD-V21). A request that resolves the session and then evaluates `@RequireOrgPermission` and `@RequireOrgMember` spends the key's quota three times (REV-BA:`probe-apikey-policy.mjs`: `requestCount` 1 → 2 → 3). On an authoritative route the key session is not accepted at all (§7.3), so one validation is spent before the 401. The **session unit** announces it, because it is the unit registered in exactly this setup (an app that uses key sessions usually never imports `./api-key`). Its `advise()` emits `W_API_KEY_SESSION_MULTIPLIER` when `context.hasPlugin('api-key')` and any referenced policy declares `presentsCredentials`, and recommends `apiKeyPrincipal()` for key traffic. The option itself cannot be read from the plugin object, so the message is conditional unless `session.apiKeySessions` states the fact (§8.3.1) `[R1:BA-r1-05]`;
  - a quota-consuming source (`effects.consumesQuota`) on a WebSocket transport with `principalTtlMs: 0` verifies on every message (`W_QUOTA_PER_MESSAGE`, §9.3).
- **Policy I/O** is deduped per request by concrete inputs (Z6): `@RequireOrgPermission(p, org A)` twice on one request is one call; for org A and org B it is two.

### 7.10 Origin check for cookie-carrying operations `[R1:SEC-r1-01, BA-r1-03]` `[R2:SEC-r2-01, SEC-r2-03, SEC-r2-05, SEC-r2-08, NEST-r2-13]`

better-auth protects cookie-bearing requests on its own routes with an origin check, and that check is **router-only**. `validateOrigin` is registered as router middleware and returns early without `ctx.request` (LEAD-V16). Every `auth.api.getSession({ headers })` the guard makes is therefore unprotected, and v1 wrongly listed "origin/CSRF" as something `auth.handler` does for the whole app. In a probe, the guard's `getSession` accepted an evil-origin cookie request that the router rejected with 403 (REV-SEC:`probe-bridge-foreign.mjs`). With better-auth's documented cross-domain cookie settings (`sameSite: 'none'`), or with an attacker on a sibling subdomain (same-site), this allowed:

- cross-site form posts to Nest routes;
- cross-site GraphQL mutations;
- Cross-Site WebSocket Hijacking (browsers attach cookies to WebSocket upgrades, CORS does not apply, and the attacker reads the replies), including GraphQL queries sent over the socket.

The kernel therefore applies **better-auth's own rules**, and only those, to the surfaces this library creates.

**No exemption better-auth does not make** `[R2:SEC-r2-01]`. v2 skipped the check when the request also carried an "explicit" credential (a `Bearer`/`DPoP` authorization, a source's credential header), on the theory that such a credential authenticated the call. It never checked that it did.
