
- **The map is §2.1, one to one.** The thirteen subpaths of §2.1 are the thirteen subpath keys here (`./package.json` aside) and the thirteen entries of §12.1 (twelve in the library build, one in the plugin build). A CI check compares the three lists, so an entry cannot ship without its export or the other way round.
- **Condition order.** Within `exports`, the most specific condition (`module-sync`) comes first. Within each branch, `types` comes first and `default` last (publint `EXPORTS_TYPES_SHOULD_BE_FIRST`, `EXPORTS_DEFAULT_SHOULD_BE_LAST`). This exact shape, packaging variant A, passed attw with all columns green and publint with only an `engines` suggestion (R:packaging §5.4).
- **Types under `module-sync`.** TypeScript ignores `module-sync` and resolves `import`/`require` to `.d.mts`/`.d.cts`, whose contents are identical.
- **Augmentations from our own subpaths.** `./api-key` adds its principal kind with `declare module 'nestjs-slightly-better-auth' { interface PrincipalKinds { … } }` inside its own declaration file (§2.2.15). That is a package self-reference from a file under `node_modules`. TypeScript resolves it through the `exports` map, and the augmentation applies only in programs that import `./api-key` (LEAD-EXP-5). The consumer type matrix asserts both directions (§12.9 step 10).
- **No default exports anywhere.** Named exports only, per publint `CJS_WITH_ESMODULE_DEFAULT_EXPORT`.
- **`sideEffects: false` is honest.** Nothing runs at import time, and no entry keeps module-level state (§12.5).
- **No `typesVersions`.** `node10` is unsupported (§11.8).

### 12.4 Engines and peers (D1, D4)

- **`engines.node: ">=22.12.0"`.** This is the require(esm) line: it is unflagged in 22.12.0, and 22.11 fails (R:packaging §1.4). Node 20 is EOL (2026-04-30). It is the floor any CJS consumer of better-auth 1.7 or Nest 12 already has, whatever we ship (R:packaging §2.6). There is no upper bound, because the reference's `<23` broke Node 24 users (#130).
- **Peers:** Nest `^11 || ^12`; `@nestjs/graphql ^13 || ^14`; `graphql ^16.11 || ^17` (both GraphQL majors peer on that range); better-auth `>=1.7.0 <2`. The table is §2.4.
- **better-auth specifiers we import.** A peer range is only as good as the subpaths it guarantees, so the list is closed and CI-checked:

  | Entry                            | better-auth specifiers (runtime)                                                                                                                                           | Verified in 1.7.4  |
  | -------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------ |
  | `.` and the Nest-facing subpaths | `better-auth/api` (`isAPIError`)                                                                                                                                           | LEAD-V2, LEAD-V5   |
  | `./plugin`                       | `better-auth/api` (`createAuthMiddleware`, `setShouldSkipSessionRefresh`), `better-auth/cookies` (`parseCookies`)                                                          | LEAD-V2, LEAD-V19  |
  | `./api-key`                      | `better-auth/plugins/access` (`role`)                                                                                                                                      | LEAD-V15           |
  | `./testing`                      | `better-auth` only; `authHeadersFor` uses the `testUtils()` plugin that the user's test instance already includes                                                          | LEAD-V15           |
  | `./testing/conformance`          | `better-auth` (`betterAuth`), `better-auth/api` (`createAuthEndpoint`, for `conformanceProbePlugin()`), `better-auth/plugins` (`testUtils`), `better-auth/adapters/memory` | LEAD-V15, LEAD-V33 |
  | declarations                     | `better-auth` (types only, §11.7)                                                                                                                                          | EXP-C11            |

  Every specifier in the table is in the `exports` map of better-auth 1.7.0 as well (LEAD-V33). The 1.7.0 floor job also loads every entry and runs the conformance kits (§14.2), so a specifier that a later release drops or moves fails our CI, not a user's boot. `@better-auth/api-key` is **not** a peer: `./api-key` calls `auth.api.verifyApiKey` and reads `$context`, and never imports the package (§2.4). It is a devDependency, installed in the matrix at the same version as better-auth.

- **Nest-owned identifiers.** The transports' handler claims and core's coverage rule read Nest metadata (§5.4 B16, §9.1–§9.4). Where Nest exports the identifier from a package root, we import it: `GRAPHQL_MODULE_OPTIONS`, `RESOLVER_TYPE_METADATA` and `RESOLVER_PROPERTY_METADATA` from `@nestjs/graphql` 13 and 14 (LEAD-V30, LEAD-V42). Where it does not, the unit that needs it holds the string literal: `'path'` and `'method'` (HTTP routes, `httpTransport()`), `'websockets:is_gateway'` (LEAD-V13) and `'websockets:message_mapping'` (the WS units), `'microservices:pattern'` (LEAD-V32), and `'__guards__'` and `'__interceptors__'` (core's coverage rule, to recognize `@UseGuards(BetterAuthGuard)` with `@UseInterceptors(BetterAuthScopeInterceptor)`) (LEAD-V42) `[R2:NEST-r2-02, NEST-r2-11, NEST-r2-12]`. There are **no deep imports** of Nest packages: 12.x packages have `exports` maps, and the specifiers differ between the two majors (LEAD-V29). Each literal is pinned by a CI test on both majors (§12.9 step 7) `[R1:NEST-r1-05, NEST-r1-06, NEST-r1-13]`.
- **No version probing** `[R1:NEST-r1-13, SEC-r1-12]`. Nothing in the package reads a Nest package's version or probes an API to infer it. A skewed install (for example `@nestjs/core` 12 with `@nestjs/websockets` 11, which package managers only warn about) therefore cannot switch a check off: gateway, hybrid-RPC and field-resolver coverage are required on every major (ADR-40). Mixed Nest majors remain unsupported. One feature detection exists, and it gates no check: the gRPC carrier uses Nest 12's `Grpc*Exception` classes when a namespace import of `@nestjs/microservices` has them, and plain `RpcException` codes otherwise (§9.4).
- **Semver.** Dropping a Node, Nest or better-auth major is a semver-major change. Format and engines never change in a minor release (#108, #130, #141). A change of the plugin protocol version (`BridgeHandle.protocol`, B04) is a semver-minor change at least, and both halves ship in the same package version.

### 12.5 Dual-package hazard strategy (S5) `[A][B][C]`

**Primary: `module-sync` first, ESM canonical (packaging variant A).** On every Node version in our engines range, `import` and `require` both resolve the `module-sync` branch, so both load the ESM build. There is exactly one copy of every class (`BetterAuthModule`, `BetterAuthGuard`, `BetterAuthService`, `WsConnectionAuth`, platform and transport classes) per process. This was verified for this exports shape on 22.12.0, 22.22.0 and 26.7.0 ("both→mjs", R:packaging §5.4). The CJS build serves tools that resolve `require` without `module-sync` support, such as some bundlers and runners, which is exactly R3's purpose. For bundlers, `default`-condition handling is UNVERIFIED and is covered by the bundler fixtures (§14.6).

**Defense in depth, independent of routing:**

1. Every DI token, metadata key and runtime slot is `Symbol.for('nestjs-slightly-better-auth:…')` (§2.3). That includes the tokens extension units export (`WS_CONNECTION_AUTH`) and the per-invocation slots (`ACTIVE_ORGANIZATION_ID`, `ACTIVE_MEMBER_ROLE`) `[R1:NEST-r1-12, NEST-r1-01]`. `Symbol()` and random `Reflector.createDecorator()` keys do not survive two copies (R:packaging §5.2: `Symbol()` tokens → `UnknownDependenciesException`; `Symbol()` metadata keys → hooks silently not discovered).
2. Class tokens have `Symbol.for` aliases (`BETTER_AUTH_SERVICE` via `useExisting`, `WS_CONNECTION_AUTH` for `WsConnectionAuth`) plus helper decorators (`@InjectBetterAuthService()`), so injection works across copies.
3. The plugin-to-kernel link is a versioned protocol object on the plugin instance, found through `getPlugin()` (§10.2). It is never shared module state.
4. Requirement metadata carries policy objects by reference, so the guard of either copy just calls `evaluate`. Principal kinds, accepted kinds and param-kind constraints are plain strings (§7.6), which compare equal across copies.
5. There is no `instanceof` on our own classes across the package boundary:
   - `isAuthFailure` (§2.2.6) checks the failure's `Symbol.for` brand, and the composition root recognizes an `ExtensionDefinition` by its `EXTENSION_DEFINITION` brand (§2.2.1), not by class;
   - our own error classes carry a `Symbol.for` brand too. The guard and `normalizeThrown` recognize `BetterAuthInfrastructureError` and `BetterAuthConfigurationError` with `isInfrastructureError` / `isConfigurationError` (§2.2.6), so an error thrown by a source or policy compiled against the other copy is passed through, not wrapped again `[R1:SEC-r1-19]`;
   - better-auth errors use `isAPIError` (S6);
   - the HTTP, WS and RPC denials are Nest's own exception classes, with one copy per Nest major. `BetterAuthGraphqlDenial` and `BetterAuthGraphqlInternalError` are read by the GraphQL drivers structurally (`extensions`), never by class.
6. There is no module-level mutable state. Everything lives in a provider, on an extension instance or on the plugin object `[R1:SEC-r1-15, SEC-r1-16, SEC-r1-18, SEC-r1-05]`:

   | State                                                                                                                                                         | Lives in                                                                                                       |
   | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
   | request, connection, invocation and browser-leg state (origin verdicts); route-plan cache per (class, handler); registries; the application's lifecycle state | kernel providers (`RequestScope`, `RoutePlanner`, `TransportRegistry`, `InstanceRegistry`, `MountCoordinator`) |
   | once-per-application flags and caps: `W_PROXY_UNTRUSTED`, the degraded-tier warning, the 100-path cap of the 404 diagnostics                                  | `AuthExchange` and the platform provider                                                                       |
   | the API-key outage-probe throttle                                                                                                                             | the `apiKeyPrincipal()` source instance                                                                        |
   | the client-IP header name, the binding, the pre-bind dispatch counter, the set of endpoint-produced results, the `initTestApp` slot                           | the plugin object returned by `nestjs()` (one per better-auth instance)                                        |

   "Once" in a warning's description therefore means once per Nest application, which is also once per process outside tests.

7. Double registration across copies is caught by the exclusive plugin binding (B06), the per-server mount stamp (B10) and the one-declaration rule for platforms and transports (B25) (§5.6).
8. CI loads both builds in one process and asserts that tokens, metadata, brands and the plugin handshake interoperate (§14.6).

**What remains.** Class identity for enhancers: `overrideProvider(BetterAuthGuard)` and `overrideGuard(BetterAuthGuard)` must import the same copy the app resolved, which `module-sync` makes automatic on supported Node. `overrideAuthGuard` from `./testing` takes the class from the library build's shared chunk, so it always matches the copy that `.` resolved in the same format (§14.8). This is documented and covered by the dual-load test.

**Rejected alternatives** (ADR-20):

- **`node` → CJS routing:** it would make every Node consumer, including Nest 12 ESM apps, run the CJS build, against better-auth's and Nest 12's ESM direction. It also needs `.d.cts` under `node.import` to avoid attw "Masquerading as ESM".
- **An ESM wrapper over CJS:** it makes CJS canonical, for the same reason.
- **ESM-only:** it violates R3.
- **Plain `import`/`require` routing:** it leaves the class-identity hazard open.

### 12.6 Decorator-metadata guarantees `[A][B][C]`

- **Explicit `@Inject(token)`** on **every** library constructor parameter, so correctness never depends on `design:paramtypes`. Isolated transpilation (oxc) emits `Object` for interface and type-only-import parameters (R:packaging §4.1). This covers the classes v2 added or made injectable for users (`WsConnectionAuth`, the extension classes behind `ExtensionDefinition.exports`).
- **`tsconfig.build.json`**, the exact file tsdown reads, sets `experimentalDecorators` and `emitDecoratorMetadata`. Without the first, tsdown **builds successfully** but emits TC39 decorator syntax that throws `SyntaxError` at load. Metadata is still emitted for users' own injectables that extend library classes.
- **CI checks:**
  - `dist/**/*.{mjs,cjs}` contains no raw `@`-decorator syntax;
  - `dist/index.mjs` contains `__decorateMetadata("design:paramtypes"`;
  - every entry is imported from `dist` in both formats, and a minimal app is booted from each.
- **Biome.** `style/useImportType` is off for `src/**`, because its "safe fix" rewrites injected classes into type imports and yields `design:paramtypes: [Object]`. `unsafeParameterDecoratorsEnabled: true`. `noUnusedPrivateClassMembers` is off for constructor-injected members. `vcs.useIgnoreFile: true`. The literal ban of §3.2 rule 5 is a Biome restricted-syntax rule scoped to `src/core/**` (§14.7) `[R1:NEST-r1-07]`.

### 12.7 Optional peers via subpaths

- The root entry imports only required peers. Every optional peer is imported **statically** and only by its own subpath: `./graphql` → `@nestjs/graphql`; `./websockets` → `@nestjs/websockets`; `./microservices` → `@nestjs/microservices`; `./testing` → `@nestjs/testing`. A REST-only app never resolves them (reference #82, #97, #100).
- `./admin` and `./organization` import the kernel only. `./api-key` adds `better-auth/plugins/access` and nothing else. The better-auth plugins themselves are the user's imports in `auth.ts`; their presence is boot-checked (B13).
- **Not used:**
  - Nest's `loadPackage`: sync and `process.exit` on failure in 11, async and internal in 12 (R:nest-di §8.1);
  - `createRequire(import.meta.url)('peer')`, which is bundler-hostile (#147);
  - bare `require`;
  - top-level await;
  - lazy `import()` on hot paths;
  - deep imports of Nest packages (`@nestjs/<pkg>/<path>`, §12.4).
- **Import-graph checks in CI:**
  - `.` must not reach an optional peer or any `src/extensions/**` file other than the built-in units the composition root re-exports (`http`, `session`);
  - `./plugin` (including its chunks) must not reach `@nestjs/*` or `node:*`; its only runtime imports are `better-auth/api`, `better-auth/cookies` and `defu`;
  - an extension must not import another extension;
  - no source file imports a Nest deep specifier, `better-call` or `@better-auth/*`.

### 12.8 Toolchain (R5)

- **pnpm.** A workspace with the library at the root and fixtures under `fixtures/*` (§14.6), each an explicit package. Because of pnpm's strict layout, every module a test imports is an explicit devDependency; the current repo's `rxjs` was unresolvable (R:current-repo). That includes `@better-auth/api-key` and the optional Nest peers, which the conformance jobs need.
- **tsdown 0.23.x**, pinned exactly with its rolldown. A caret pairing produced hashed `.d.ts` names in the current repo.
- **TypeScript 6.x** as the devDependency. rolldown-plugin-dts's `tsc` generator needs the classic JS API that TS 7 lacks (R:packaging §2.4).
- **vitest 5 on Vite 8.** It honors `emitDecoratorMetadata` from tsconfig without `unplugin-swc` (R:packaging §4.3). Vite 8 is pinned. The security suite runs as its own vitest project with `NODE_ENV=production` (§14.4), because better-auth switches its origin checks off under `NODE_ENV=test`.
- **biome**, with the rules in §12.6.
- **lefthook** pre-commit: `biome check` and `tsc --noEmit`. A tsdown build succeeds despite type errors, so the separate typecheck is mandatory.
- **Release:** changesets and npm OIDC trusted publishing with provenance.

## 13. Error model

### 13.1 Taxonomy `[A][B][C]`

| Class                                                | When                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                           | Status                                                                                       | `code` / `reason`                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                               | Logged                                                                                      |
| ---------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| **Denial: unauthenticated**                          | required route, no principal (including an authoritative route that met a session a hook supplied, §7.3); a policy's better-auth call answered 401 and the principal no longer resolves (§8.1)                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                 | 401                                                                                          | `UNAUTHENTICATED`; `reason` = better-auth's code where one exists                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                               | no (debug)                                                                                  |
| **Denial: rejected credential**                      | a source returned `rejected` (for example an `APIError` 401/403 from `getSession` hooks, a bad JWT, an API key reported invalid, disabled or expired)                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          | 401 or 403 (better-auth's status)                                                            | `UNAUTHENTICATED` / `FORBIDDEN`; `reason` = better-auth `body.code` (`INVALID_API_KEY`, `KEY_EXPIRED`, `UNAUTHORIZED`, …)                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       | no (debug)                                                                                  |
| **Denial: forbidden**                                | a policy, the acceptance gate, a param-kind constraint or the origin check denied                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              | 403 (401 for `USER_NOT_FOUND`, or when a policy asks for re-authentication with a challenge) | `FORBIDDEN` / `UNAUTHENTICATED`; `reason` ∈ `MISSING_PERMISSION`, `INSUFFICIENT_SCOPE`, `USER_IS_NOT_A_MEMBER_OF_THE_ORGANIZATION`, `YOU_ARE_NOT_A_MEMBER_OF_THIS_ORGANIZATION`, `NO_ACTIVE_ORGANIZATION` (better-auth's membership codes, passed through by the org policies, §8.3), `ORGANIZATION_REQUIRED`, `SESSION_NOT_FRESH`, `PRINCIPAL_NOT_SUPPORTED`, `USER_REQUIRED`, `USER_NOT_FOUND`, `INVALID_ORIGIN`, `MISSING_OR_NULL_ORIGIN`, `CROSS_SITE_NAVIGATION_LOGIN_BLOCKED` (§7.10), better-auth codes, extension codes | no (debug)                                                                                  |
| **Denial: rate limited**                             | better-auth 429 during resolution or evaluation, or `verifyApiKey` reporting `RATE_LIMITED`/`USAGE_EXCEEDED`                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                   | 429                                                                                          | `RATE_LIMITED`; `reason` = the better-auth code; `Retry-After` from the error's headers or `details.tryAgainIn`                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                 | no (debug)                                                                                  |
| **Infrastructure** (`BetterAuthInfrastructureError`) | any throw from a source, policy or better-auth call that is not a 401/403/429 `APIError`: storage or network failure, `APIError` ≥ 500, `BetterAuthError`, an API-key outage detected by the probe (a failing read or no-op write); a 401 from a policy's better-auth call while the principal still resolves authoritatively (§8.1); a failing function-valued `trustedOrigins` (§7.10); `auth.handler` throwing on auth routes                                                                                                                                               | 500                                                                                          | HTTP: Nest's default 500 body; GraphQL `INTERNAL_SERVER_ERROR` with `reason: 'AUTH_UNAVAILABLE'` and a generic message; WS/RPC "Internal server error"                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          | **yes**, once, by Nest's exception layer (not intrinsic), with a **redacted** cause (§13.4) |
| **Configuration** (`BetterAuthConfigurationError`)   | boot validation (§5.4); at request time: no transport for a context, unresolved policy, `userId` mapper returning `null`, another 4xx `APIError` from our own call, a principal or invocation param decorator with no authentication result or published value (`NO_AUTH_RESULT`, `NO_INVOCATION_VALUE`, §7.8), `BetterAuthService.getPrincipal()` outside any handler scope (`NO_AUTH_SCOPE`), an HTTP adapter that appeared after the core module initialized (`LATE_HTTP_ADAPTER`, §5.7), and any of these raised through `BetterAuthService` in a handler or resolver body | boot: the process fails; request time: 500                                                   | `code` = the check id (e.g. `NO_TRANSPORT`, `UNRESOLVED_POLICY`, `NO_AUTH_RESULT`). Request-time errors are created with `atRequest`: `message` is `Authentication is misconfigured` and site, detail and hint are own properties, so a client never sees them, whether a transport mapped the error (guard) or not (decorators, services). On GraphQL the client sees only `reason: 'AUTH_MISCONFIGURED'` and a generic message `[R1:SEC-r1-19]`                                                                               | yes (Nest's exception layer prints `detail`, `site` and `hint`, LEAD-V31)                   |
| **Auth routes**                                      | anything better-auth returns                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                   | verbatim                                                                                     | better-auth's `{ message, code }` bodies; ours only for `PAYLOAD_TOO_LARGE` (413) and `INVALID_REQUEST_URL` (400), in the same shape; with `onAPIError.throw`, the user's filters decide                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        | host pipeline for 5xx and rethrown `APIError`s                                              |

**The key rule (S6).** Only a _denial value_ produces 401, 403 or 429. Detection uses `isAPIError` from `better-auth/api` (LEAD-V5), the status comes from `e.statusCode`, and the reason from `e.body?.code`. For `verifyApiKey`, which returns failures as values, the mapping is an explicit table with an outage probe (§8.3.1). Nothing in the library catches an arbitrary error and returns 401/403. The reference did that for every plugin error (R:ref-impl §6.1).

### 13.2 Normalization `[B][C]`

Sources and policies return values. The kernel's safety net normalizes anything they throw:

```ts
/** A policy's better-auth call answered 401: the evaluator re-resolves the principal before it answers 401 or 5xx (§8.1). */
type SessionLossCandidate = {
  readonly sessionLoss: unknown;
  readonly reason?: string;
};
function normalizeThrown(
  e: unknown,
  where: "source" | "policy",
  site: string,
  secrets: readonly string[],
): AuthFailure | SessionLossCandidate | never {
  if (isAuthFailure(e)) return e; // brand check, dual-package safe
  if (isInfrastructureError(e) || isConfigurationError(e)) throw e; // already classified (e.g. SESSION_USER_ID, the API-key outage probe): never re-wrapped
  if (isAPIError(e)) {
    // better-auth/api; never instanceof (S6)
    const status = e.statusCode,
      reason = (e.body as { code?: string } | undefined)?.code;
    if (status === 429) return AuthFailures.fromAPIError(e)!; // Retry-After from headers or body.details.tryAgainIn
    if (status === 401 && where === "policy") return { sessionLoss: e, reason }; // §8.1: the evaluator re-resolves before it answers 401 or 5xx [R2:BA-r2-03]
    if (status === 401 || status === 403)
      return where === "source"
        ? AuthFailures.rejected({ status, reason }) // presented credential rejected
        : AuthFailures.forbidden(reason ?? "FORBIDDEN"); // principal is authenticated → 403
    if (status >= 500) throw new BetterAuthInfrastructureError(e, { secrets });
    throw BetterAuthConfigurationError.atRequest(
      "BETTER_AUTH_REJECTED_CALL",
      `better-auth rejected the library's call (${status} ${reason})`,
      { site },
    );
  }
  throw new BetterAuthInfrastructureError(e, { secrets });
}
```

A 4xx other than 401, 403 or 429 means our own call was malformed, for example a validation error from `userHasPermission`. That is a bug or a misconfiguration, not a client error `[C]`. Built-in policies convert the better-auth outcomes they expect into decisions themselves before this net sees them:

- `USER_IS_NOT_A_MEMBER_OF_THE_ORGANIZATION` (401 → 403);
- `YOU_ARE_NOT_A_MEMBER_OF_THIS_ORGANIZATION` (403 → 403, as a decision rather than a thrown error);
- `NO_ACTIVE_ORGANIZATION` and `MEMBER_NOT_FOUND` (400) from `getActiveMember` in the default organization ref → no organization, 403 `NO_ACTIVE_ORGANIZATION` (§8.3);
- the admin endpoint's `user not found` (400 → 401 `USER_NOT_FOUND`, §8.3) `[R1:BA-r1-10]`.

A source never gets the re-classification: a source's 401 is a rejected credential. A policy's generic 401 (`UNAUTHORIZED`, or none) always goes through it, because the principal was authenticated a moment before and better-auth's session middleware cannot tell a lost session from a failed read (LEAD-V36).

### 13.3 Mapping per transport and payload contract

```ts
/** HTTP body of a denial: Nest's default shape plus a stable code. [A][C] */
export interface AuthErrorBody {
  statusCode: 401 | 403 | 429;
  error: string;
  code: AuthErrorCode;
  reason?: string;
  message: string;
}
/** GraphQL extensions of a denial or an internal error (both drivers). [L] */
export interface AuthGraphqlExtensions {
  code: AuthErrorCode | "INTERNAL_SERVER_ERROR";
  reason?: string;
  statusCode: number;
}
/** WS and RPC error object. [A][B][C] */
export interface AuthTransportErrorPayload {
  status: "error";
  statusCode: number;
  code: AuthErrorCode;
  reason?: string;
  message: string;
}
```

| Transport                   | Denial thrown                                                                                                                                     | Client-visible payload                                                                                                                                                                                                                                   | Infrastructure / configuration at request time                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              |
| --------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| HTTP                        | `UnauthorizedException` / `ForbiddenException` / `HttpException(…, 429)` constructed with `AuthErrorBody` and `{ cause }` (intrinsic: not logged) | `{ "statusCode": 403, "error": "Forbidden", "code": "FORBIDDEN", "reason": "MISSING_PERMISSION", "message": "Forbidden" }` + `WWW-Authenticate` when a challenge exists + `Retry-After` for 429. User filters catching `ForbiddenException` keep working | the error itself: Nest's filters answer a generic 500 and log it (redacted cause)                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                           |
| GraphQL (Apollo, Mercurius) | `BetterAuthGraphqlDenial` (intrinsic, `extensions`) (LEAD-EXP-1)                                                                                  | `errors[i].extensions = { code, reason, statusCode }`, HTTP 200; identical across drivers; same codes Apollo uses for 401/403                                                                                                                            | from the guard: `BetterAuthGraphqlInternalError` via `toInternalException`: message `Internal server error`, `extensions.code = 'INTERNAL_SERVER_ERROR'`, `reason` `AUTH_UNAVAILABLE` / `AUTH_MISCONFIGURED`. Thrown where no transport maps it (a param decorator whose guard did not run, `BetterAuthService` in a resolver body): the error as thrown, `Authentication is misconfigured` / `Authentication service unavailable` with the same `extensions` (LEAD-EXP-7). Details only in the server log `[R1:SEC-r1-19]` |
| WebSocket                   | `WsException(AuthTransportErrorPayload)`                                                                                                          | `exception` event with that object (`BaseWsExceptionFilter`)                                                                                                                                                                                             | "Internal server error", logged                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                             |
| RPC                         | `RpcException(AuthTransportErrorPayload)`                                                                                                         | that object (`BaseRpcExceptionFilter`)                                                                                                                                                                                                                   | "Internal server error", logged                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                             |
| gRPC (carrier)              | `RpcException({ code: 16 \| 7 \| 8, message })` or Nest 12's `Grpc*Exception`                                                                     | gRPC status + message                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    | status 13                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                   |
| Auth routes                 | better-auth's own responses, untouched                                                                                                            | better-auth's `{ message, code }`                                                                                                                                                                                                                        | 500 via the host pipeline                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                   |

**Errors thrown outside the guard** `[R1:SEC-r1-19]`. Param decorators (§7.8) and `BetterAuthService` run where the guard's transport mapping does not, so their errors reach each runtime unmapped: Nest's default 500 on HTTP, `Internal server error` on WS and RPC, and the error's own `message` and `extensions` on GraphQL. Both library error classes are therefore generic as thrown: a request-time `BetterAuthConfigurationError` (`atRequest`) and `BetterAuthInfrastructureError` carry a fixed message and `extensions` with the reason, and keep the specifics in own properties (`detail`, `site`, `hint`, the redacted `cause`) that neither GraphQL driver serializes (LEAD-EXP-7).

`AuthFailure` is transport-neutral, and only a transport's `toException` knows the transport's format. A new transport therefore gets the whole taxonomy by implementing one method, plus `toInternalException` if its runtime would expose error messages `[B]`.

### 13.4 Logging and redaction `[R1:SEC-r1-08]`

- **Denials are not errors.** HTTP and GraphQL mappings are `IntrinsicException`s, which Nest's filters do not log (LEAD-V9). Denials, origin-check failures included, are logged at `debug` by the guard.
- **Infrastructure failures are logged once per request, by Nest's exception layer, with a redacted cause.** Nest's `ConsoleLogger.error(err)` prints `util.inspect(err)`, which includes the `[cause]` chain and enumerable properties (LEAD-V31); pino/nestjs-pino serializers and Sentry's linked-errors integration read `error.cause` too. Driver errors commonly embed query parameters: drizzle-orm 0.45.2 builds `DrizzleQueryError` with the message `` `Failed query: ${query}\nparams: ${params}` `` (`errors.js:10-16`), and `findSession(token)` puts the session token in those params. v1 attached the raw cause, so a database timeout would have shipped live session and bearer tokens to log aggregators for every guarded request during the outage.

  v2's `ErrorRedactor` (U18) builds the cause instead:
  - **Secrets** are the request's credential values:
    - every cookie value in the `Cookie` header, and its URL-decoded form;
    - for signed values (`token.signature`), the part before the last `.` when at least 16 characters long, which is the form stored in the database;
    - the `authorization` value and its credential part after the scheme;
    - the values of every declared credential header (source `credentialHeaders`, e.g. `x-api-key`).
  - **The redacted cause** is a new `Error` with the original's `name` and its `code`, `errno` and `syscall` when present. Its message is the **first line** of the original message, truncated to 300 characters, with every secret replaced by `[REDACTED]`. Its `stack` is that header plus the original stack frames (frames are file positions only). Nested causes are redacted the same way, to a depth of 3.
  - **The raw cause** is kept under a non-enumerable `Symbol.for('nestjs-slightly-better-auth:raw-cause')` slot, which `util.inspect` does not print. It is reachable through `getRawCause(error)` only when `errors.exposeRawCause: true` (local debugging).
  - The same redaction applies on auth routes (`AuthExchange` knows the inbound credentials) and on the `WsConnectionAuth` path.

- **Never logged:** request headers, `Cookie`, `Set-Cookie`, bearer tokens and API keys. One alternative library logs full headers (R:ba-integrations §6.6). A hygiene conformance case (`S-log-redaction`) makes an adapter throw with the session token in its message and asserts the token never appears in captured logs.
- **better-auth's own logger** is outside this library's control. It logs `Failed to validate API key:` with the underlying error at ERROR for every failed key verification (LEAD-V20), and it logs origin failures at ERROR on auth routes. The docs recommend configuring better-auth's `logger` (level, or a redacting `log` function) in production (RK19).
- The docs warn that with `apiKey({ enableSessionForAPIKeys })`, the mocked session carries the raw key in `session.token`. Serializing `@CurrentSession()` into responses or logs leaks it (R:ba-authz §1.2). `apiKeyPrincipal()` never exposes the raw key.

### 13.5 Customization

```ts
export interface ErrorMappingOptions {
  /** Replace what a transport throws for a denial; return undefined to keep the transport's default. [C] */
  map?: (
    failure: AuthFailure,
    context: ExecutionContext,
    transport: string,
  ) => unknown;
  /** Keep the unredacted cause reachable through getRawCause() (local debugging only). Default false. [R1:SEC-r1-08] */
  exposeRawCause?: boolean;
}
```

- `errors.map` is a per-instance override: a runtime option (§5.2) of the instance whose plan produced the denial (§5.5). It is applied before the transport's `toException`, and receives the transport's id (§9.0).
- A deeper change is made by subclassing a transport (for example the HTTP transport) and listing it in `transports`, where it is selected before the built-in one `[A]`.
- Neither mechanism depends on exception filters, which do not reach WebSocket gateways in any Nest version (R:nest-di §5.2).

## 14. Testing strategy

### 14.1 Conformance kits (the LSP proof, reusable by third parties) `[A][B][C]`

The kits live in `nestjs-slightly-better-auth/testing/conformance`. They are **runner-agnostic**: each returns `ConformanceCase[]`, and `runConformance(cases, { describe, it })` registers them with vitest, jest or `node:test`. Assertions use `node:assert/strict`. The same kits run in our CI for every built-in unit, which makes "Express and Fastify behave the same" a tested property rather than a claim.

Each HTTP case boots a real Nest app, under both `NestFactory.create` and `Test.createTestingModule().createNestApplication()`. It uses a real better-auth instance (memory adapter) that includes `conformanceProbePlugin()`, which provides these endpoints:

- `/probe/echo-raw`: `disableBody` + `ctx.request.text()`, echoing the received bytes and headers;
- `/probe/multi-cookie`: three cookies;
- `/probe/redirect`: 302 with a cookie;
- `/probe/stream`: three chunks with delays;
- `/probe/html`;
- `/probe/put`, `/probe/patch`, `/probe/delete`;
- `/probe/url`: echoes `request.url`;
- `/probe/ip`: echoes `getIP(request)`;
- `/probe/throw-api-error`, `/probe/throw-error`.

The probe plugin also contributes a trusted origin through `init()` (`https://probe-plugin.example`), so trusted-origin cases exercise the post-init set (LEAD-V17). The kit also adds a throwing `around` interceptor, an app controller `/app/echo` that returns `{ body, rawBody }`, and a global `APP_FILTER` that records what it sees.

```ts
export interface HttpConformanceOptions {
  platform: ExtensionRef<HttpPlatform>;
  /** Fresh Nest HTTP adapter per app, e.g. () => new ExpressAdapter(). */
  createHttpAdapter(): AbstractHttpAdapter;
  /** Bootstraps to exercise. Default both. */
  bootstrap?: readonly ("factory" | "testing")[];
  /** Enable host CORS the platform's usual way. Default: app.enableCors({ origin, credentials: true }). */
  enableHostCors?(app: INestApplication, origin: string): void | Promise<void>;
  /** Configure trust in one forwarding hop the platform's usual way (for H-proxy-trust / H-url-trust-proxy). */
  trustOneProxy?(app: INestApplication): void | Promise<void>;
  /** HTTP/2 variant, required when the platform declares capabilities.http2. */
  http2?: { createHttpAdapter(): AbstractHttpAdapter };
  /** How to obtain a base URL. Default: app.listen(0) + getUrl(). */
  listen?(app: INestApplication): Promise<string>;
}
export interface TransportConformanceOptions {
  transport: ExtensionRef<AuthTransport>;
  /**
   * Boots an app exposing the kit's fixture handlers (TransportFixtures: 'required', 'optional', 'public', 'forbidden', 'triple',
   * 'tripleMixed', 'readsSession', 'unsafe', 'loginProxy', 'publicService', 'acceptsApiKey', 'org', 'inherited', 'unguarded', and
   * 'graph' for GraphQL shapes) in the transport's shape, with BetterAuthModule's globalGuard set as given. Handlers receive the default
   * instance's BetterAuthService (FixtureContext), injected with @Inject(BETTER_AUTH_SERVICE). With globalGuard: true the harness adds
   * what its shape needs for coverage (a gateway class carries @UseBetterAuth()); with false it adds nothing, and the kit adds
   * @UseBetterAuth() or @UseGuards(BetterAuthGuard) to a fixture's decorators where a case asks for it. When `override` is given, the harness
   * boots through Test.createTestingModule() and passes the builder through it before compile(). The kit boots [R2:NEST-r2-02]:
   *   1. with globalGuard: true, for every case that serves requests;
   *   2. with globalGuard: true and override = (b) => overrideAuthGuard(b, passThrough), a stand-in guard that returns true and
   *      stamps nothing (§14.8), for the 'unguarded' part of T-internal-error-generic: B16 sees every handler covered, yet the
   *      param decorators find no result, a path no coverage check can see (§7.8 item 4);
   *   3. with globalGuard: false, only for T-coverage-claims, whose boots are expected to fail and serve no request.
   */
  createApp(
    fixtures: TransportFixtures,
    auth: AuthLike,
    options: {
      globalGuard: boolean;
      override?: (builder: TestingModuleBuilder) => TestingModuleBuilder;
    },
  ): Promise<INestApplication>;
  /** Invokes a fixture handler with given credentials and browser headers; returns the transport-native outcome. */
  invoke(
    app: INestApplication,
    handler: Exclude<keyof TransportFixtures, "graph">,
    headers: HeadersInit,
    input?: Record<string, unknown>,
  ): Promise<{
    ok: boolean;
    body?: unknown;
    error?: {
      code?: string;
      statusCode?: number;
      reason?: string;
      message?: string;
    };
    setCookies: string[];
  }>;
  /**
   * Two invocations of the 'org' fixture in ONE logical request or connection, with different inputs, in the given shape:
   * 'aliases': two aliased GraphQL root fields in one operation; 'batched': two operations in one batched GraphQL HTTP request;
   * 'messages': two messages on one WS socket (principalTtlMs > 0); 'subscriptions': two GraphQL subscriptions on one connection
   * (subscriptionPrincipalTtlMs > 0 and 0). The kit calls it once per entry of invocationShapes. [R1:NEST-r1-01]
   */
  invokeTwice?(
    app: INestApplication,
    shape: InvocationShape,
    inputs: [Record<string, unknown>, Record<string, unknown>],
    headers: HeadersInit,
  ): Promise<
    [
      { ok: boolean; error?: { reason?: string } },
      { ok: boolean; error?: { reason?: string } },
    ]
  >;
  /** Shapes invokeTwice can produce; required with it. Apollo and Mercurius: ['aliases', 'batched', 'subscriptions']; socket.io and ws: ['messages']. */
  invocationShapes?: readonly InvocationShape[];
  /**
   * GraphQL shapes: one operation over HTTP selecting the given root fields of fixtures.graph, in order, each with the given
   * FixtureNode fields; the harness serves 'graph' with fieldResolverEnhancers: ['guards', 'interceptors']. It runs T-stamp-per-plan
   * and T-inherit-no-lookup. Without it both cases are skipped with a reason, unless the transport defines defaultAccessFor, in which
   * case they fail. [R2:NEST-r2-04, NEST-r2-06]
   */
  invokeGraph?(
    app: INestApplication,
    selection: readonly GraphSelection[],
    headers: HeadersInit,
  ): Promise<{
    data: unknown;
    errors: readonly {
      path: readonly (string | number)[];
      code?: string;
      reason?: string;
      message?: string;
    }[];
  }>;
  expectCookieCapable: boolean;
  /** Whether the transport has a browser leg (false for RPC): enables the T-csrf-* cases. */
  expectBrowserLeg: boolean;
}
export type InvocationShape =
  "aliases" | "batched" | "messages" | "subscriptions";
/** One fixture handler the kit supplies; the harness exposes it as a controller route, resolver field, gateway message or message pattern. */
export interface FixtureHandler {
  /** Method decorators to apply, in order (access, acceptance, requirements). */
  readonly decorators: readonly MethodDecorator[];
  /** Parameter decorators by parameter index, e.g. [CurrentSession()]. */
  readonly params: readonly ParameterDecorator[];
  /** 'read': HTTP GET, GraphQL query, RPC request. 'unsafe': HTTP POST, GraphQL mutation. WS messages are always enforced (§7.10). */
  readonly operation: "read" | "unsafe";
  /** Handler body: receives the decorated parameter values, the invocation input and the harness context; its result is the response. */
  handle(
    params: readonly unknown[],
    input: Record<string, unknown>,
    context: FixtureContext,
  ): unknown;
}
/** What the harness hands every fixture handler. [R2:SEC-r2-04] */
export interface FixtureContext {
  /** The default instance's service (BETTER_AUTH_SERVICE): loginProxy calls service.api.signInEmail, publicService calls getSession(). */
  readonly service: BetterAuthService;
}
/**
 * GraphQL shapes only: one object type FixtureNode, returned by three root fields and carrying three field resolvers, served with
 * fieldResolverEnhancers: ['guards', 'interceptors'] (T-stamp-per-plan, T-inherit-no-lookup). [R2:NEST-r2-04, NEST-r2-06, SEC-r2-09]
 */
export interface GraphFixtures {
  readonly roots: {
    readonly public: FixtureHandler; // @Public(); no params
    readonly sessionOnly: FixtureHandler; // default kinds; @CurrentPrincipal()
    readonly mixed: FixtureHandler; // @AcceptPrincipals('session', 'api-key'); @CurrentPrincipal()
  };
  readonly fields: {
    readonly plain: FixtureHandler; // no metadata, no params: an 'inherit' plan
    readonly reader: FixtureHandler; // no access, acceptance or requirement metadata; @CurrentPrincipal(): an 'inherit' plan
    readonly guarded: FixtureHandler; // @RequireAuth(): a real plan, enforced per field
  };
}
export interface GraphSelection {
  readonly root: keyof GraphFixtures["roots"];
  readonly fields: readonly (keyof GraphFixtures["fields"])[];
}
/** The fixture handlers of transportConformance, by name (the `handler` argument of invoke()). */
export interface TransportFixtures {
  readonly required: FixtureHandler; // default access; returns the principal's kind (T-no-credentials, T-credentials, T-acceptance, T-infra-5xx)
  readonly optional: FixtureHandler; // @OptionalAuth()
  readonly public: FixtureHandler; // @Public() (T-public-no-lookup)
  readonly forbidden: FixtureHandler; // a requirement whose kit policy always denies (T-error-shape, T-no-error-log)
  /** Three DISTINCT handler methods with equal accepted kinds, invoked in one logical request, e.g. 3 root fields in 3 resolver methods: 1 resolution (T-memo-once, S7). [R2:NEST-r2-16] */
  readonly triple: readonly [FixtureHandler, FixtureHandler, FixtureHandler];
  /** Like triple, but the second method adds @AcceptPrincipals('session', 'api-key'): exactly 2 resolutions. */
  readonly tripleMixed: readonly [
    FixtureHandler,
    FixtureHandler,
    FixtureHandler,
  ];
  readonly readsSession: FixtureHandler; // @CurrentSession() (T-reads-session, T-carrier / T-scope)
  readonly unsafe: FixtureHandler; // operation 'unsafe' (T-csrf-*)
  readonly loginProxy: FixtureHandler; // @Public() @ForwardAuthCookies(), operation 'unsafe', calls service.api.signInEmail (T-csrf-login-proxy, T-coverage-claims) [R2:SEC-r2-08]
  readonly publicService: FixtureHandler; // @Public(), operation 'unsafe', returns service.getSession() (T-public-service-null) [R2:SEC-r2-04]
  readonly acceptsApiKey: FixtureHandler; // @AcceptPrincipals('session', 'api-key') (T-credentials)
  readonly org: FixtureHandler; // orgPermission(p, { organization: fromParam('orgId') }) + @ActiveOrganizationId() (T-invocation-decisions, Z-org-ref-types)
  /** One method of an abstract base class, exposed through two subclasses: one @Public(), one with the kit's always-deny requirement (T-inherited-handler). [R2:NEST-r2-01] */
  readonly inherited: FixtureHandler;
  /** @CurrentSession() + @ActiveOrganizationId(), no access metadata; served in boot 2, where a stand-in guard stamps nothing (T-internal-error-generic). [R2:NEST-r2-02] */
  readonly unguarded: FixtureHandler;
  /** GraphQL shapes only; other harnesses ignore it. [R2:NEST-r2-04, NEST-r2-06] */
  readonly graph: GraphFixtures;
}
export interface PrincipalSourceConformanceOptions {
  source: ExtensionRef<PrincipalSource>;
  credentials: {
    valid(): Promise<Headers>;
    invalid(): Headers;
    rateLimited?(): Promise<Headers>;
  };
}
export interface PolicyConformanceOptions {
  requirement: RequirementExpr;
  allowingPrincipal(): Promise<AuthPrincipal>;
  denyingPrincipal(): Promise<AuthPrincipal>;
  delegatedPrincipal?(): Promise<AuthPrincipal>;
}
```

**HTTP platform cases** (invariants H1–H13, §4.1.2):

Each clause names its case id; §4.1.2 maps the ids to invariants, except the cases listed after the table. Every case runs under both bootstraps and on Nest 11 and 12, which is how H9 is checked for the whole suite.

| Group       | Cases (id)                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                             |
| ----------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Mount       | every method (GET, POST, PUT, PATCH, DELETE, HEAD, OPTIONS, QUERY if supported) reaches better-auth under the base path (`H-mount-methods`); the bare base path reaches it, `/api/authx` falls through, and a controller outside the path still works (`H-mount-boundary`); custom path via a `baseURL` path, via `basePath`, and via dynamic `allowedHosts` + `basePath`, and a Nest global prefix + URI versioning leave the mount unchanged (`H-mount-custom-path`); a controller route under the path wins (`H-app-route-precedence`, H11)                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                         |
| Body        | byte-exact echo, one case per content shape (the `H-body-*` family): JSON with odd whitespace and key order (`H-body-json`), UTF-8 (`H-body-utf8`), urlencoded `b=%20x&c=1` (`H-body-urlencoded`), `text/plain` (`H-body-text`), `application/scim+json` (`H-body-scim`), multipart (`H-body-multipart`), binary (`H-body-binary`), chunked transfer (`H-body-chunked`), empty body (`H-body-empty`), no content-type (`H-body-no-content-type`), and a urlencoded sign-in that succeeds (`H-body-form-sign-in`). Over-limit → 413 **with host CORS headers** for a declared `content-length` (`H-limit-declared`) and a chunked body (`H-limit-chunked`), with the canonical body, byte-identical across platforms and exact at the boundary (`H-limit-canonical-body`). App routes are still parsed, with `useBodyParser` limits (`H-app-parsing`), and keep `rawBody` (`H-app-rawbody`)                             |
| Facts       | URL protocol and host honor the platform's trust-proxy setting (`H-url-trust-proxy`); the query string is preserved, OAuth `?code=&state=` (`H-url-query`); percent-encoding is kept (`H-url-encoded`); `Origin`, `Referer`, `Sec-Fetch-*`, `Cookie`, `Authorization` and `Content-Type` arrive unmodified (`H-headers-passthrough`); better-auth's `getIP` sees the platform IP, with per-IP rate-limit buckets in production mode, and a variant with better-auth's `advanced.ipAddress.trustedProxies` covering the proxy: trust off gives no IP plus the B18 warning, trust on gives the client IP (`H-ip-platform`) `[R2:BA-r2-04]`; a client-sent client-IP header (fixed name or any `x-nsba-ip-*`) is ignored (`H-ip-spoof`); `proxyTrust()` reports the effective setting before and after `trustOneProxy` (`H-proxy-trust`); HTTP/2 pseudo-headers do not crash, h2c with capability `http2` (`H-h2-pseudo`) |
| Write-back  | three `Set-Cookie` preserved on separate lines (`H-resp-multicookie`); 302 + `Location` + cookie, not followed (`H-resp-redirect`); a 3-chunk stream arrives in order and a client abort cancels the reader (`H-resp-stream`); HEAD has no body and never 500s (`H-resp-head`); status and headers are written verbatim, `text/html` passes through, `vary` is merged, and a before-hook `APIError` becomes its Response (`H-resp-status`); host CORS answers the preflight (`H-cors-preflight`) and adds its headers to real responses (`H-cors-actual`); `requests.key()` is the same object for guards, interceptors and GraphQL of one request (`H-accessor-key`); cookies written through `cookieSink()` arrive alongside the handler's own, and `cache-control`/`pragma` from `getSession` never leak onto app routes (`H-accessor-cookie-merge`)                                                                |
| Errors      | a non-`APIError` from `auth.handler` reaches the host pipeline as a 5xx (`H-errors-infra`), and the kit's global filter sees it and Nest logs it, with a global prefix set (`H-errors-filter-sees`, the Fastify awaited-registration case of LEAD-EXP-2); with `onAPIError.throw`, the filter receives the original `APIError` (`H-errors-apierror-throw`); no hang, every request completes within a timeout (`H-errors-no-hang`)                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                     |
| Lifecycle   | `MiddlewareConsumer` middleware runs before the auth handler, no global prefix (`H-middleware-order`); a `forRootAsync` factory awaiting an async dependency still captures bytes under `NestFactory` (`H-async-options-factory`); `createMicroservice` and `createApplicationContext` through `NestFactory`, `Test…compile()` + `moduleRef.init()`, and `Test…createNestMicroservice()` boot without platform calls, each microservice once with `listen()` and once with `init()` then `listen()` (lifecycle work runs once, no `INSTANCE_ALREADY_BOUND`) (`H-no-adapter`) `[R2:NEST-r2-05, NEST-r2-09]`; `moduleRef.init()` followed by `createNestApplication().init()` fails with `LATE_HTTP_ADAPTER` (`H-late-adapter`); a second `forRoot` for the same instance → boot error (`H-double-forroot`); unbind on `app.close()` (`H-unbind-on-close`)                                                               |
| Diagnostics | a 404 under the mount logs one WARN with a "did you mean" outside production and never changes the response (`H-diagnostics-404`); `W_PROXY_UNTRUSTED` once in production with forwarding headers and trust off (`H-proxy-untrusted-warning`)                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          |
| Hygiene     | probe cookies never appear in captured logs (`H-log-hygiene`)                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          |

`H-no-adapter`, `H-late-adapter`, `H-double-forroot`, `H-unbind-on-close`, `H-diagnostics-404`, `H-proxy-untrusted-warning` and `H-log-hygiene` map to no platform invariant (§4.1.2). They check behavior that core provides around every platform: the mount coordinator's and instance registry's lifecycle (§5.7, B06, B07), 404 diagnostics (ADR-52), the proxy-trust warning built on `proxyTrust()` (§6.8) and log redaction (§13.4). They run in the platform kit so that each platform's bootstraps and error paths exercise them.

**Transport cases** (invariants T1–T10):

| Id                                             | Asserts                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              |
| ---------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `T-selection`                                  | `handles()` is true only for its contexts, with and without credentials                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              |
| `T-public-unclaimed-context`                   | a `@Public()` handler in a context type no registered transport handles (the kit registers a custom context type through `ExternalContextCreator`) runs, and the guard does no auth work; a required one answers `NO_TRANSPORT` `[R2:NEST-r2-03]`                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    |
| `T-no-credentials`                             | missing credentials → 401 `UNAUTHENTICATED`, no throw from `headers()`; for RPC, a TCP message with a primitive payload and one without an `auth` object → 401 on a required handler, success on a public one `[R2:NEST-r2-03]`                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      |
| `T-credentials`                                | cookie, bearer (bearer plugin) and `x-api-key` credentials are extracted                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                             |
| `T-memo-once`                                  | at most one `getSession` per key under N guard invocations: `triple`, three distinct handler methods with equal accepted kinds (GraphQL: 3 root fields in 3 resolver methods) → 1 call (S7); `tripleMixed` → 2 calls `[R2:NEST-r2-16]`. With the `'subscriptions'` shape: two subscriptions on one connection resolve the principal twice with `subscriptionPrincipalTtlMs: 0` and once with a TTL, on Apollo and on Mercurius; the same for two queries sent over the graphql-ws socket and over Mercurius `fullWsTransport`, under Nest's default and a custom Apollo context; an authoritative plan resolves per operation even with a TTL `[R2:SEC-r2-03, SEC-r2-07]`                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            |

`T-credentials`, `T-acceptance`, `T-infra-5xx`, `T-public-no-lookup`, `T-public-unclaimed-context`, `T-public-service-null`, `T-reads-session`, `T-inherited-handler` and `T-scope` map to no transport invariant (§4.2.2): they check behavior that core provides on top of T1–T10 (S6, per-route acceptance of principal kinds (ADR-35), `@Public()` doing no I/O, B15, the plan cache, the decorators' scope) through each transport, and `T-subscription-credentials` gates a preview feature.

**Principal-source cases** (P1–P6: `S-*`) and **policy cases** (Z1–Z6: `Z-*`) are smaller harnesses around a real instance, using the memory adapter plus better-auth's `testUtils()` (LEAD-V15). The instance runs with `session.updateAge: 0`, so any session-reading endpoint a unit calls produces a refresh `Set-Cookie`. The generic cases run against any source or policy:
